definition_zh: 州长；总督；管理者
definition_en: the elected head of a state, a colonial ruler, or a member of a governing board
core_image: 一位身穿深色西装的人在新修的道路旁与工程师交谈，身后是州旗
scene: 州长视察了新修的道路。 The governor visited the new road.
sceneCN: 这里 governor 是「州长」（第 1 个义项）；句意：州长视察了新修的道路。

senses.title: Head of a state
senses.definition: the elected head of a state in a federal country
senses.definitionCN: 联邦制国家中民选的州最高行政长官
senses.example: The governor visited the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 州长视察了新修的道路。
senses.why: This is the most familiar modern sense in the United States.
senses.whyCN: 这是美国现代最常见、最熟悉的含义。

senses.title: Colonial ruler
senses.definition: a person appointed to rule a colony or province
senses.definitionCN: 被任命统治殖民地或行省的人
senses.example: The governor ruled the colony for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 那位总督统治该殖民地十年。
senses.why: Older empires used the word for appointed rulers abroad.
senses.whyCN: 旧帝国用这个词指在外地受任的统治者。

senses.title: Member of a board
senses.definition: a member of a board that governs an institution
senses.definitionCN: 管理某机构的董事会成员
senses.example: She was appointed a governor of the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为这家医院的董事。
senses.why: Schools, banks, and hospitals also have governors.
senses.whyCN: 学校、银行和医院也有 governor。

definition_zh: 视力；景象；名胜
definition_en: the ability to see, something seen, or a famous place
core_image: 远处一座塔忽然进入视野，眼睛一下亮起来
scene: 天一黑，她的视力就明显变差。 Her sight is poor at night.
sceneCN: 这里 sight 是「视力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她晚上的视力很差。

senses.title: The ability to see
senses.definition: the power of seeing
senses.definitionCN: 看见东西的能力
senses.example: Her sight is poor at night.
senses.exampleCN: 她晚上的视力很差。
senses.why: This is the basic ability sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的能力义项。

senses.title: Something seen
senses.definition: a thing that you see, often striking
senses.definitionCN: 看到的景物，常指引人注目的
senses.example: The mountain came into sight.
senses.exampleCN: 那座山出现在视野中。
senses.why: What the eyes catch becomes a sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛捕捉到的东西就成了景象。

senses.title: A famous place
senses.definition: a famous or interesting place visited by tourists
senses.definitionCN: 游客参观的著名或有趣的地方
senses.example: We visited the sights of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 我们参观了这座城市的名胜。
senses.why: Places worth seeing are called sights.
senses.whyCN: 值得一看的地方被称为名胜。

abstract.en: Sight turns distance into nearness.

abstract.en: What we see shapes what we believe.

abstract.en: Some things are a sight for sore eyes.

definition_zh: 直接地；径直地；立即
definition_en: in a straight or immediate way, with nothing in between
core_image: 一束光穿过敞开的窗，直直落在桌面，不碰墙也不拐弯
scene: 窗子正对着太阳，光一路照到桌中央。 The road runs directly to the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 directly 指「径直地」（第 1 个义项：不绕路）；句意是这条路直通港口。

senses.title: By a straight path
senses.definition: along a line with no turn and nothing in the way
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条不拐弯、也没有遮挡的线
senses.example: The road runs directly to the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路直通港口。
senses.why: The shortest path is also the least eventful.
senses.whyCN: 最短的路线，也是最没有故事的一条。

senses.title: With no one in between
senses.definition: done by the person or thing itself, without another hand
senses.definitionCN: 由本人或本物完成，中间不经别人的手
senses.example: You can speak directly to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以直接和经理谈。
senses.why: A chain of hands slows every message and changes it.
senses.whyCN: 一串手递过去，消息既变慢也变形。

senses.title: At once, without delay
senses.definition: immediately after something happens
senses.definitionCN: 在事情发生后马上
senses.example: She left directly after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会议一结束她就走了。
senses.why: No turn in space becomes no gap in time.
senses.whyCN: 空间上不拐弯，就变成了时间上不留缝。

intro.en: Directly is direct plus the adverb ending -ly, built on Latin dirigere, to guide straight.
intro.cn: directly 是 direct 加副词词尾 -ly，词根是拉丁语 dirigere（拉直、引导）。

items.en: Regere meant to guide or to keep straight.
items.cn: regere 指引导，也指保持笔直。

items.en: Directus described something set in a straight line.
items.cn: directus 形容被摆成直线的东西。

items.en: English direct meant straight and plain.
items.cn: 英语 direct 指笔直与直白。

items.en: The ending -ly made it describe the manner of an action.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 让它转而描述动作的方式。

items.en: It added the time sense of immediately, and a conjunction use.
items.cn: 它又添上「立即」的时间义，并发展出连词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct- stem, while the meaning group covers straightness, immediacy and personal action.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 词干，近义组则覆盖径直、立即与亲自。

normal.en: Direct plus -ly: the adjective learns to describe how.

normal.en: A direct road and a direct answer both skip the scenery.
normal.cn: 直路与直话，都省掉了沿途的风景。

abstract.en: Picture a beam landing on a table without touching the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光落在桌上，没有碰到墙。

abstract.en: Picture two people talking with nobody seated between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人说话，中间没坐别人。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing behind the last guest at once.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一位客人一出门，门就关上了。

examples.en: The train goes directly to the city centre.
examples.cn: 这趟火车直达市中心。

examples.en: I heard the news directly from her.
examples.cn: 这消息是我直接从她那里听来的。

examples.en: He called directly after the letter arrived.
examples.cn: 信一到他就打了电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 directly 记成「地雷克特利」：地上有雷，得看准一条直线，径直穿过去。

root: 由 direct 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，词根可追到拉丁语 dirigere（拉直、引导），由 dis- 与 regere 组成。它修饰动作，表示沿直线、不经中间人，或在时间上紧接着发生；英式英语里还发展出连词用法，表示「一……就」。

sensesIntro.en: From a path with no turn, to a word with no middleman, to a moment with no gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条不拐弯的路，到一句不经中间人的话，再到一个不留缝的时刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light crossing an open window and landing straight on a table.

branches.en: The first sense is the straight line in space.

branches.en: The second sense removes the middleman from an action.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把中间人从动作里拿掉。

branches.en: The third sense removes the gap in time.
branches.cn: 第三个义项拿掉了时间上的缝隙。

branches.en: A straight path and a direct word both refuse detours.
branches.cn: 直路与直话，都拒绝绕行。

branches.en: No middleman and no delay are the same impatience.

definition_zh: 正式地；形式上；郑重地

senses.title: Officially

senses.example: The president formally announced the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 总统正式宣布了决定。
senses.why: This is the main public sense.

senses.title: According to form

senses.title: Politely

definition_zh: 容易；轻松；舒适；安逸；缓解；减轻；放松
definition_en: freedom from difficulty or discomfort; also to relieve pain, loosen something, or move it gently
core_image: 老木匠闭着眼推刨子，木屑卷成均匀的卷
scene: 老木匠闭着眼推刨子，木屑卷成均匀的卷。 She eased the drawer open without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 ease 是「缓缓地使（某物）松开、移动」（第 5 个义项：轻缓地移动或打开）；句意为她无声地把抽屉缓缓拉开。图中可辨识物件：刨子、木屑、抽屉。

pos.zh: 名词：容易；轻松；舒适；安逸
动词：缓解；减轻；放松；缓缓移动

forms.label: 复数（名词，指多种轻松状态）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「容易；轻松」
由否定前缀与本词构成，义为「不安；焦虑」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「安适的；轻松的」

senses.title: Freedom from difficulty
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to do, so that little effort is needed
senses.definitionCN: 做起来容易、不需要多少力气的性质
senses.example: She lifted the crate with ease.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻松地就把木箱提了起来。
senses.why: The word came from comfort and opportunity; something within reach is something done without strain, and that became ease.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指舒适与便利：在掌握之内的事做起来不费劲，这种不费劲就成了 ease。

senses.title: Comfort and freedom from strain
senses.titleCN: 舒适：身体或心情不受紧张
senses.definition: a state of bodily or mental comfort, without pain, worry or tension
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心理舒适，没有疼痛、忧虑或紧张的状态
senses.example: The warm bath put him at ease after the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶后，热水澡让他放松下来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a body settled into a fitting place, with nothing pressing against it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：身体安顿在合适的位置里，没有任何东西压着它。

senses.title: To relieve pain
senses.definition: to make pain, discomfort or a bad feeling less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使疼痛、不适或糟糕的感觉变得不那么严重
senses.example: The ointment eased the burn within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 药膏几分钟内就缓解了灼痛。
senses.why: Comfort as a state becomes an action: you remove the pressure that kept the body from settling.
senses.whyCN: 当「舒适」作为一种状态转为动作：你移开了那个让身体无法安顿的压力。

senses.title: To loosen or relax
senses.definition: to make something less tight, less tense or less firmly fixed
senses.definitionCN: 使某物不那么紧、不那么绷、不那么牢固
senses.example: Ease the belt after the meal.
senses.exampleCN: 饭后把腰带松一松。
senses.why: A tight thing is under strain, and easing it restores the slack that comfort requires.
senses.whyCN: 紧的东西处在张力之下，ease 就是把它恢复成舒适所需要的松弛。

senses.title: To move something gently
senses.titleCN: 轻缓地移动：慢慢把某物移开或打开
senses.definition: to move someone or something slowly and carefully into or out of a place
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物缓慢小心地移进或移出某个位置
senses.example: She eased the drawer open without a sound.
senses.exampleCN: 她无声地把抽屉缓缓拉开。
senses.why: Careful movement avoids strain, so the verb that removes strain also describes motion done without a jolt.
senses.whyCN: 小心的移动能避开张力，于是表示「去除张力」的动词也用来描述不带顿挫的动作。

intro.en: Ease came into English from Old French, and its deeper origin has been debated rather than settled.
intro.cn: ease 经由古法语进入英语，其更早来源一直有争论而无定论。

items.en: Aise meant comfort, convenience and room to act, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: aise 意为舒适、便利、有余地，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: One common explanation links aise to Latin adiacens, 'lying near'; other sources propose different origins, so the question is uncertain.
items.cn: 一种常见解释把 aise 联系到拉丁语 adiacens「邻近的」；也有资料提出别的来源，因此此事尚无定论。

items.en: The noun ease entered English and quickly added the senses of comfort and freedom from difficulty.
items.cn: 名词 ease 进入英语后，很快加上了「舒适」与「不费力」两义。

items.en: The verb developed from the noun, first as relieve and loosen, then as move gently.
items.cn: 动词由名词发展而来，先有「缓解、放松」，再引申为「轻缓移动」。

items.en: With ease, at ease and ease off fixed the word in everyday speech, while technical uses appeared in mechanics.
items.cn: with ease、at ease、ease off 把词固定在日常语言中，机械领域也出现了技术用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that differ by one sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for comfort and relief.
note.cn: 形近组收只差一个音的小词；近义组收表示舒适与缓解的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning not difficult or not causing strain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「容易的、不费力的」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning without difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「容易地、毫不费力地」。

entries.definition: The direction of the sunrise, with no link to comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 日出的方向，与「舒适」无关。

entries.definition: A state of physical ease and freedom from pain, or a thing that gives it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体舒适、无痛的状态，或带来这种状态的东西。

entries.definition: The removal or reduction of pain, worry or pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 疼痛、忧虑或压力的消除或减轻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a body at rest to the hand that loosens a belt and opens a drawer without noise.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从休息中的身体，走到那只松开腰带、无声拉开抽屉的手。

normal.en: Ease begins as a body that fits its place, then becomes a task that fits your strength.
normal.cn: ease 起初是身体适合所处的空间，后来成了任务适合你的力气。

normal.en: With ease turns the noun into an adverb: no strain visible on the face.
normal.cn: with ease 把名词变成副词：脸上看不出一点吃力。

normal.en: To ease pain is to take away what was pressing on the body.
normal.cn: ease pain 就是把压在身体上的东西移开。

normal.en: A belt, a knot and a screw are all eased by giving them back a little slack.
normal.cn: 腰带、绳结与螺丝，都是靠还回一点松弛来 ease 的。

normal.en: Ease a drawer open means moving it so gently that it never jolts.
normal.cn: ease a drawer open 指把抽屉移得极轻，轻到从不顿一下。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a tight knot, slowly letting one loop go loose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在紧结上，慢慢让一个环松开。

abstract.en: The same loosening can happen in a shoulder, a rule, a market or a drawer.
abstract.cn: 同一种「松开」可以发生在肩膀、规则、市场或抽屉上。

abstract.en: Ease means the pressure is reduced until motion becomes quiet.
abstract.cn: ease 意味着压力被减到动作变得安静为止。

examples.en: She lifted the crate with ease.
examples.cn: 她轻松地就把木箱提了起来。

examples.en: The warm bath put him at ease after the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途驾驶后，热水澡让他放松下来。

examples.en: She eased the drawer open without a sound.
examples.cn: 她无声地把抽屉缓缓拉开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「意兹」——闭着眼推刨子，木屑卷得均匀

root: ease 经由古法语 aise「舒适、便利」进入英语；其更早来源有拉丁语 adiacens「邻近」等多种解释，尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of ease all reduce strain: no difficulty, bodily comfort, less pain, a looser fit, and a motion made quiet.
sensesIntro.cn: ease 的五个义项都在减少张力：不费力、身体舒适、疼痛减轻、配合变松，以及变得安静的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand slowly loosens one loop of a tight knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手慢慢松开紧结上的一个环。

branches.en: THE TASK: what fits your strength is done without strain.
branches.cn: 任务线：适合你力气的事，做起来就不费劲。

branches.en: THE BODY: comfort is the original sense, a body settled with nothing pressing it.
branches.cn: 身体线：舒适是最初的义项，身体安顿下来，没有东西压着。

branches.en: THE RELIEF: the state becomes an action that removes pain.
branches.cn: 缓解线：状态转为动作，把疼痛移走。

branches.en: THE SLACK: a tight thing is given room again.
branches.cn: 松弛线：紧的东西重新获得余地。

branches.en: THE QUIET MOTION: strain-free movement is movement without a jolt.
branches.cn: 静动线：没有张力的移动，就是不带顿挫的移动。

intro.en: Ease is a French borrowing; English expands it with suffixes and a negative prefix rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: ease 是法语借词，英语用后缀与否定前缀来扩展它，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: A Latin link to adiacens has been proposed but not established, so it is presented as one explanation among several.
latinIntro.cn: 有人提出与拉丁语 adiacens 的联系，但并未确立，因此只作为若干解释之一。

items.example: The French noun is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词是直接来源。

definition_zh: 配偶；（动物）配对的对象；伙伴；朋友（英式口语）；交配；配对
definition_en: a partner in a pair, especially for breeding, or to pair with such a partner
core_image: 两只海鸟年复一年在同一块礁石上重逢，替对方理掉颈羽上的盐粒，再合筑一个巢
scene: 两只海鸟年复一年在同一块礁石上重逢，替对方理去颈羽上的盐粒，再合筑一个巢。 Two seabirds meet again on the same rock year after year, preen the salt from each other's neck feathers, and build one nest: each has found a mate for life.
sceneCN: 这里 mate 指「长期共同繁殖的配偶」（第 1 个义项：配偶、配对对象）；句意为两只海鸟年年重逢、互相理羽并合筑一巢，各自找到了终生的配偶。可辨识物件：礁石、相互理羽的两只鸟、同一个巢、海水；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 伙伴；朋友（英式口语，尤用于男性之间）

senses.title: A partner in a breeding pair
senses.definition: one of the two animals or people that form a reproductive pair
senses.definitionCN: 构成繁殖配对的两只动物或两个人之一
senses.example: The male guards the nest while his mate feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 雄性看守巢，配偶外出觅食。
senses.why: The word began as 'one who shares food at the same table', and that image of a shared life became the image of a shared nest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「同桌共食的人」，那幅共享生活的图景后来变成共享巢的图景。

senses.title: A spouse or long-term partner
senses.definition: a husband, wife or long-term romantic partner
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫、妻子或长期恋人
senses.example: He introduced her as his mate, not his girlfriend.
senses.exampleCN: 他介绍她是自己的伴侣，而不是女友。
senses.why: From the 1540s the noun named one of a married pair, and that sense remains the plainest one in many varieties of English.
senses.whyCN: 自 16 世纪 40 年代起，这个名词指已婚一对中的一方，这一义项在许多英语变体中仍是最平实的。

senses.title: A comrade or friend
senses.definition: a friend, especially a male friend addressed informally
senses.definitionCN: 朋友，尤指被随意称呼的男性朋友
senses.example: He turned up with two old mates from the docks.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着两个码头上的老朋友来了。
senses.why: The oldest sense was 'associate, fellow', and it survives in British informal speech long after the breeding sense took over in biology.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「同伴、伙计」，在生物学中繁殖义占主导之后，它仍存活于英式口语中。

senses.title: To pair for breeding
senses.definition: of animals, to come together in order to reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 动物为繁殖而结合在一起
senses.example: The two species rarely mate in the wild.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在野外很少交配。
senses.why: The verb, recorded about 1600 in this sense, simply turned the noun into an action: to become a pair.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在该义项约自 1600 年有记录，只是把名词变成动作：成为一对。

senses.title: To match two things
senses.definition: to join two things that belong together, such as parts or colours
senses.definitionCN: 把两个相配之物接合起来，如零件或颜色
senses.example: The two halves must be mated before the glue sets.
senses.exampleCN: 两半必须在胶凝固之前对接。
senses.why: If a mate is a matching partner, then to mate is to make two things into such a pair, even when neither is alive.
senses.whyCN: 如果 mate 是相配的伙伴，那么 to mate 就是把两物做成这样一对，即便两者都不是活物。

senses.title: A ship's officer
senses.definition: an officer on a merchant ship ranking below the master
senses.definitionCN: 商船上低于船长的驾驶员
senses.example: The mate checked the cargo before departure.
senses.exampleCN: 大副在开船前检查了货物。
senses.why: Shipboard hierarchy borrowed the word for a companion officer, and the rank survives in merchant and fishing fleets.
senses.whyCN: 船上的等级制度借用了这个表示同伴官员的词，这一职衔至今仍存于商船与渔船队。

senses.title: An assistant tradesman
senses.definition: a skilled worker's assistant in a trade, as in plumber's mate
senses.definitionCN: 行业熟练工的助手，如管道工的副手
senses.example: The plumber's mate fetched the right joint.
senses.exampleCN: 管道工的助手取来了合适的接头。
senses.why: In a trade the partner is the one who works alongside, so the word names a role rather than a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 在手艺行当里，伙伴就是并肩干活的人，因此这个词命名一种角色，而非一段关系。

senses.title: Abstract: one of a matched pair
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：相配一对中的一方
senses.definition: one of two things that correspond to each other, such as a glove or a shoe
senses.definitionCN: 彼此对应的两物之一，如手套或鞋
senses.example: He held up the left glove and asked where its mate was.
senses.exampleCN: 他举起左手的手套，问另一只在哪里。
senses.why: At its widest the word needs no animal and no friend: anything that completes a pair can be its mate.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词既不需要动物，也不需要朋友：任何补成一对的东西都能是它的 mate。

intro.en: Mate is a Germanic borrowing, not a Latin word. Middle Low German mate, gemate meant 'one eating at the same table', and English took it in the mid-fourteenth century as 'companion'.
intro.cn: mate 是日耳曼语借词，并非拉丁词。中低地德语 mate、gemate 意为「同桌进食的人」，英语在 14 世纪中叶把它借作「同伴」。

items.en: The compound *ga-matjon meant '(one) having food (*matiz) together (*ga-)'. The same *matiz lies behind English meat.
items.cn: 复合词 *ga-matjon 意为「共同（*ga-）拥有食物（*matiz）的人」。同一个 *matiz 也是英语 meat 的来源。

items.en: Middle Low German mate, gemate 'messmate, companion' is the immediate source, cognate with Dutch maat and German Maat.
items.cn: 中低地德语 mate、gemate「同餐伙伴、同伴」是直接来源，与荷兰语 maat、德语 Maat 同源。

items.en: English mate is recorded from the mid-fourteenth century meaning 'associate, fellow', and as a form of address among sailors and workers.
items.cn: 英语 mate 自 14 世纪中叶有记录，义为「伙伴、伙计」，并在水手与工人间用作称呼。

items.en: The sense 'one of a married pair' is recorded from the 1540s; the verb 'to pair, couple' from about 1500, with the animal sense from about 1600.
items.cn: 「已婚一对中的一方」义自 16 世纪 40 年代有记录；动词「配对、结合」约自 1500 年，动物交配义约自 1600 年。

items.en: The mate of checkmate is a different word: it comes through Old French from Persian shah mat 'the king is helpless'.
items.cn: checkmate 中的 mate 是另一个词：经古法语来自波斯语 shah mat「王已无路可走」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the reconstruction of *matiz and its wider Indo-European links is debated, and the exact first date of the nautical rank is not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*matiz 的重构及其更广的印欧语联系存有争论；航海职衔的确切首见年代也无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the verb forms, the informal adjective and the unrelated chess word; group two holds nouns for a partner under different descriptions.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词形式、口语形容词与无关的国际象棋词；第二组是以不同描述指伴侣的名词。

entries.definition: The gerund of the verb: the act or period of pairing.
entries.definitionCN: 该动词的动名词：配对的动作或时期。

entries.definition: British informal 'friendly', built on the companion sense; it has no biological meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语「友好的」，建立在同伴义上；无生物学含义。

entries.definition: A fellow member of a class; the second element still means companion, not breeding partner.
entries.definitionCN: 同班成员；第二个成分仍是「同伴」，而非繁殖配偶。

entries.definition: From Persian shah mat 'the king is helpless': a chess term with no connection to companion or spouse.
entries.definitionCN: 来自波斯语 shah mat「王已无路可走」：国际象棋术语，与同伴或配偶无关。

entries.definition: A person one shares an activity, business or life with; wider than mate and often less biological.
entries.definitionCN: 共同从事活动、事业或生活的人；比 mate 更宽，常少些生物学色彩。

entries.definition: A husband or wife in a legal marriage; mate can be used far more loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 合法婚姻中的丈夫或妻子；mate 的用法远为宽松。

entries.definition: Someone who accompanies another; from Latin panis 'bread', the very image behind mate.
entries.definitionCN: 陪伴他人的人；来自拉丁 panis「面包」，正是 mate 背后的图景。

entries.definition: A person or thing holding the same role elsewhere; it stresses correspondence, not companionship.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处担任同样角色的人或物；强调对应，而非陪伴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mate came from a word for a table companion, so a mate is literally one who shares the table.
normal.cn: mate 来自「同桌的人」，所以配偶字面上就是共享餐桌的人。

normal.en: The family runs mate, mating, mated, matey, classmate, roommate, soulmate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mate、mating、mated、matey、classmate、roommate、soulmate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mate for life, find a mate, choose a mate, mate with.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：终生配对、寻找配偶、选择配偶、与……交配。

normal.en: Checkmate looks like a relative but comes from Persian.
normal.cn: checkmate 看似同族，其实来自波斯语。

normal.en: The nautical rank survives in merchant ships: the chief mate is below the master.
normal.cn: 航海职衔仍存于商船：大副在船长之下。

abstract.en: Picture two birds sharing one rock as if it were one table.
abstract.cn: 想象两只鸟共用一个礁石，仿佛那是同一张餐桌。

abstract.en: Picture a left glove waiting in a drawer for its other half.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里一只左手手套等着另一半。

abstract.en: Picture two parts that were machined to meet and cannot mistake each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个被加工成彼此相合、不会认错的零件。

examples.en: The pair stays together for several seasons, mating on the same ledge.
examples.cn: 这一对会相伴数季，在同一处岩架上交配。

examples.en: He came to the party with an old mate from school.
examples.cn: 他带着一位老同学来参加聚会。

examples.en: She could not find the mate to that earring.
examples.cn: 她找不到那只耳环的另一只。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mate（同桌的人）」——先同桌吃饭，后同巢育雏 → 伙伴、配偶

root: 中低地德语 mate/gemate「同桌共食者」← 原始日耳曼 *ga-matjon（*ga- 共同 + *matiz 食物）；与拉丁语无关，与 checkmate（波斯语 shah mat）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one word from a table companion to a breeding partner, a spouse, a friend, an act of pairing, a mechanical fit, a ship's officer, an assistant, and finally either half of any pair.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一个词：从同桌的伙伴，到繁殖配偶、配偶、朋友、配对动作、机械配合、船上大副、行业助手，最后是任何一对中的任一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lives sharing one place, one table or one nest.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条生命共用一处地方、一张桌子或一个巢。

branches.en: SHARED LIFE: the biological partner, then the married one.
branches.cn: 共享生活：先是生物学配偶，再是婚姻配偶。

branches.en: SHARED WORK: the comrade at large, and the assistant in a trade.
branches.cn: 共享工作：广义的伙伴，以及行当中的助手。

branches.en: BECOMING A PAIR: animals pair, and parts are made to fit.
branches.cn: 成为一对：动物配对，零件被做成相合。

branches.en: A ROLE ON SHIP: the companion officer of the master.
branches.cn: 船上的角色：船长的同伴官员。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: anything that completes a pair.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何补成一对的东西。

intro.en: Mate is a Germanic noun and verb with no Latin element; its compounds are all native formations, which makes the word a good test of etymological honesty.
intro.cn: mate 是日耳曼语名词与动词，不含拉丁成分；其复合词都是本族构成，因此这个词很适合检验词源诚实度。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries: mate is Germanic, and the apparent Latin neighbours (as in checkmate) come from Persian. Latin supplied nothing here.
latinIntro.cn: 不列拉丁词条：mate 属日耳曼语，看似拉丁的近邻（如 checkmate）来自波斯语。拉丁语在此没有贡献。

items.example: The mated birds returned to the same ledge.
items.exampleCN: 已配对的鸟回到同一处岩架。
交配在固定展示之后发生。
他同伴般的态度很有帮助。

definition_zh: 航空公司；航线；空中直线距离；供气软管
definition_en: a company that carries passengers and goods on regular flights, the routes it flies, a straight line between two places, or a hose that supplies air
core_image: 机尾上同一枚标志，把一座座城市连成一条空中线路
scene: 清晨的候机大厅里，屏幕上的目的地一行行向上翻动，登机口前的人拖着箱子排成弯队。 The airline added two morning flights between the two cities last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 airline 是「航空公司」（第 1 个义项：经营定期航班的公司）；句意为这家航空公司去年春天在两座城市之间加开了两个早班航班。画面里是候机大厅、翻动的航班屏与排队登机的旅客。

pos.zh: 名词：航空公司；航线；直线距离；供气软管

derivatives.zh: 由 airline 加名词后缀 -er 构成（也有人把它看作 air 加 liner 的组合），义为「班机；大型客机」
由 airline 加后缀 -wide 构成，义为「覆盖整个航空公司的」，如全公司范围的罢工或规定

senses.title: A company that runs regular flights
senses.titleCN: 航空公司：经营定期航班的公司
senses.definition: a business that owns or leases aircraft and carries passengers or goods on scheduled flights
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或租用飞机、按定期航班运送旅客或货物的企业
senses.example: The airline flies to more than forty cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司飞往四十多座城市。
senses.why: An airline is literally a line in the air: a company whose business is to keep aircraft moving along fixed routes, so the route and the firm share one name.
senses.whyCN: airline 字面就是「空中的一条线」：公司的生意正是让飞机沿着固定路线往返，于是「线」和「经营这条线的公司」共用一个词。

senses.title: A route flown by aircraft
senses.titleCN: 航线：飞机定期往返的空中路线
senses.definition: a route, or a set of routes, over which aircraft travel regularly between places
senses.definitionCN: 飞机定期往返于两地之间的空中路线，或这类路线的集合
senses.example: The new airline across the mountains cuts the journey to an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这条翻越群山的新航线把行程缩短到一小时。
senses.why: Before it named a company, the word named the path itself, a line drawn in the air between two points, and this old sense still lives in the route meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在指公司之前，这个词先指路线本身，即空中连接两点的线；这层古老意思仍保留在「航线」义里。

senses.title: A straight line between two points
senses.titleCN: 空中直线：两点之间的直线距离
senses.definition: a straight line between two places, especially as a measure of distance on a map
senses.definitionCN: 两地之间的直线，尤指在地图上量出的直线距离
senses.example: The airline distance between the two ports is under thirty miles.
senses.exampleCN: 两港之间的直线距离不到三十英里。
senses.why: A line in the air ignores roads and hills, so airline came to mean the shortest straight path, the distance measured as the crow flies.
senses.whyCN: 空中的线绕开道路与山丘，于是 airline 转而表示最短的直线路径，也就是「直线距离」。

senses.title: A hose that carries air
senses.titleCN: 供气软管：输送压缩空气的管子
senses.definition: a flexible tube that supplies air, as to a diver or to a pneumatic tool
senses.definitionCN: 向潜水员或气动工具等输送空气的软管
senses.example: The diver checked the airline before entering the water.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员下水前检查了供气管。
senses.why: Here the line is a physical tube rather than a route, and the air inside it is the thing being carried; the same compound simply names a line for air.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 line 是实体的管子而非路线，里面输送的东西正是 air；同一个复合词只是把「线」落实为「管」。

intro.en: Airline is a modern English compound of air, a Greek word that reached English through Latin and French, and line, a Latin word for a linen thread.
intro.cn: airline 是现代英语复合词，由 air 与 line 构成：air 是希腊词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语；line 源自拉丁语，本指亚麻线。

items.en: Greek aer named the lower, misty air; Latin borrowed it as aer, and it kept the sense of the open sky.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指下层带雾的空气；拉丁语借作 aer，保留了「开阔天空」的意思。

items.en: Old French air carried the word into English, where air means both the gas we breathe and the open space above the ground.
items.cn: 古法语 air 把这个词带入英语，air 既指我们呼吸的气体，也指地面之上的空间。

items.en: Linea meant a linen thread and, by extension, any line; it came from linum, the word for flax.
items.cn: linea 本指亚麻线，引申为任何线条；它来自表示亚麻的 linum。

items.en: The compound air line is recorded in the early nineteenth century for a straight line or direct route; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合形式 air line 在十九世纪初有记录，指直线或直飞路线；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: With powered flight the word shifted to aviation: first an air route, then a company flying it. The hose sense belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 随着动力飞行出现，这个词转向航空：先指航线，再指经营航线的公司；软管义属于二十世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the two halves of the compound and the words built on them; the near-meaning group holds the words for carriers, journeys and routes in the same field.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两半以及由它们构成的词；近义组收同一领域里表示承运者、航班与路线的词。

entries.definition: A large passenger aircraft flown by an airline; formed from airline with the suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「班机、大型客机」，指航空公司营运的客机，由 airline 加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A route for aircraft, or a passage for air; built from air plus way, the same first half as airline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航路」或「气道」，由 air 加 way 构成，前半与 airline 相同。

entries.definition: The mixture of gases we breathe and the open sky; the first element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空气、天空」，是这个复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: A long thin mark or a row of things; the second element, from Latin linea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「线、行列」，是这个词的后半部分，源自拉丁语 linea。

entries.definition: The price of a plane ticket; another compound that uses air for aviation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机票钱」，是另一个用 air 表示航空的复合词。

entries.definition: A company that transports passengers or goods, used in official and industry language for an airline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承运人、运输公司」，在官方与行业用语中可指航空公司。

entries.definition: A single journey by air; the airline is the company, the flight is the trip it sells.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航班、飞行」，airline 是公司，flight 是公司卖出的那一趟行程。

entries.definition: A fixed path between two places; the general word behind the route sense of airline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「路线」，是 airline 表示航线时背后那个更一般的词。

entries.definition: The industry and practice of flying aircraft; broader than one company or one route.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航空、航空业」，比一家公司或一条航线更宽泛。

entries.definition: A service that travels back and forth between two places at short intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穿梭班机、短途往返班车」，指在两地之间频繁往返的服务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound, its recorded history and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词真实的两半、有记录的词源，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Air is the medium and line is the path: an airline is a line drawn through the sky.
normal.cn: air 是介质，line 是路径：airline 就是画在天空里的一条线。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the route, not the company; the firm is named after the line it flies.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是航线而不是公司；公司是照着它飞的那条线命名的。

normal.en: Airliner adds -er to name the aircraft, so airline is the firm and airliner is the plane.
normal.cn: airliner 加 -er 指飞机，所以 airline 是公司，airliner 是客机。

normal.en: Airfare, airway and airmail all use air in the same aviation sense.
normal.cn: airfare、airway、airmail 里的 air 都取同一个航空义。

normal.en: In airline distance the word means a straight line, the path a bird would take.
normal.cn: 在 airline distance 里，这个词指直线，也就是鸟飞的那条路。

abstract.en: Picture a map with two dots and one thin line between them; then picture a plane flying exactly along that line.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上两个点之间的一条细线，再想象一架飞机正沿着这条线飞。

abstract.en: The line can thicken into a company: offices, crews, timetables, all gathered around that one path.
abstract.cn: 这条线可以变粗成为一家公司：办公室、机组、时刻表都围着这条路径聚拢。

abstract.en: The same word can be a tube on a diver's back, because it too is a line that carries air.
abstract.cn: 同一个词也可以是潜水员背上的管子，因为它同样是一条输送空气的线。

examples.en: The airline cancelled the evening flight because of the storm.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司因暴风雨取消了晚间航班。

examples.en: Budget airlines have made short trips much cheaper.
examples.cn: 廉价航空公司让短途出行便宜了很多。

examples.en: He has worked as an airline pilot for twelve years.
examples.cn: 他做民航飞行员已经十二年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔莱恩」——爱尔在天上，莱恩是一条线：把城市连成一条空中线路的公司。

root: air 来自希腊语 aer「下层空气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；line 来自拉丁语 linea「亚麻线」，由 linum「亚麻」派生。十九世纪英语把两者合成 air line，先指空中的直线与直飞路径，二十世纪民航兴起后，又指经营定期航班的公司。

sensesIntro.en: One image runs through all four senses: a line drawn through the air, which can be a company flying it, the route itself, a straight distance, or a tube carrying air.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用一幅画面：一条画在空中的线，它可以属于经营航线的公司，可以是航线本身、直线距离，也可以是输送空气的管子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line is drawn across a map from one city to another, and an aircraft follows it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上从一座城市到另一座城市画出一条细线，一架飞机正沿着它飞行。

branches.en: THE FIRM: the line becomes a business with aircraft, crews and timetables.
branches.cn: 公司线：这条线变成一门生意，有了飞机、机组与时刻表。

branches.en: THE PATH: the route itself, flown regularly between two places.
branches.cn: 路径线：路线本身，在两地之间定期飞行。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the same line taken as the shortest distance on a map.
branches.cn: 测量线：同一条线被当作地图上的最短距离。

branches.en: THE TUBE: the line turns solid and carries air to a diver or a tool.
branches.cn: 管子线：这条线变成实体，把空气送到潜水员或工具那里。

branches.en: THE NAME: the company is named after the route it flies, which is why one word covers both.
branches.cn: 命名线：公司照着它所飞的航线取名，所以一个词同时覆盖两者。

intro.en: Airline is a compound whose two halves are old words; English then adds ordinary suffixes and combining forms to extend the family.
intro.cn: airline 是一个由两个古老词构成的复合词；英语再用普通后缀与组合形式扩展出这一族词。

latinIntro.en: Only the line half has Latin ancestors: linea and linum are recorded; aer came into Latin from Greek and is listed with that note.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 line 这一半有拉丁语祖先：linea 与 linum 均有记录；aer 是从希腊语进入拉丁语的，列入时已加说明。

items.exampleCN: 它提供 airline 的前半部分。

items.example: Latin aer is the ancestor of English air.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 aer 是英语 air 的祖先。

items.meaning: a cord, a row, a route
items.example: It supplies the second half of airline.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 airline 的后半部分。

items.example: Linea is the source of English line.
items.exampleCN: linea 是英语 line 的来源。

items.example: Linum is the plant behind linea.
items.exampleCN: linum 是 linea 背后的那种植物。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.exampleCN: 它由 airline 构成 airliner。

items.example: It appears in airfare and airway.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 airfare 与 airway 里。

由 airline 加后缀 -wide 构成，义为「覆盖整个航空公司的」

definition_zh: 发射；发起；推出；（船）下水；发射活动；（产品的）发布
definition_en: to send a ship, rocket or product into motion or into the market, and the act of starting something new
core_image: 船坞闸门打开，新船顺着滑道冲向水面
scene: 码头上挤满了来看新船下水的人。 The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 launch 指「使船下水」（第 1 个义项）；句意为船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。图中可辨识物件：船坞闸门、滑道、围观的人群。

collocations.phrase: the launch of a new service

derivatives.zh: 由 launch 加 -er 构成，指发射装置或发射者
由 launch 与 pad 复合，指发射台、起飞平台
由 re- 加 launch 构成，指重新推出、再次发起

senses.title: To send a newly built ship into the water
senses.definition: to move a newly built boat from the slipway into the water for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 把新造的船第一次从滑道送入水中
senses.example: The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。
senses.why: The word began as a lance thrown forward, so the first maritime use pictured a hull driven down a slipway like a weapon released.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指向前掷出的长矛，因此最早的船舶用法把船体沿滑道冲下，想象成一件被放出的武器。

senses.title: To start an activity, company or product
senses.definition: to begin something new such as a business, a campaign or a product, and make it public
senses.definitionCN: 开始并公开推出企业、运动或产品等新事物
senses.example: The company will launch its new phone next month.
senses.exampleCN: 公司下个月将推出新手机。
senses.why: Starting a venture is like setting a ship afloat: both release something built in private into the open, where it must stay afloat on its own.
senses.whyCN: 开创一项事业就像让船下水：两者都把在内部造好的东西放出去，此后它必须自己浮在水面上。

senses.title: To send a rocket or spacecraft into the air
senses.definition: to send a rocket, missile or spacecraft up into the sky or into space
senses.definitionCN: 把火箭、导弹或航天器送上天空或太空
senses.example: They launched the satellite from a desert site.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在沙漠场地发射了那颗卫星。
senses.why: A rocket is thrown upward the way a lance was thrown, and the old image of a forceful release fits the modern machine exactly.
senses.whyCN: 火箭被向上抛出，正如长矛被掷出，那个「用力放出」的旧画面恰好贴合现代机器。

senses.title: The act of launching something
senses.definition: the event or act of starting, releasing or putting something into service, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 启动、放出或让某物投入使用的活动，作名词
senses.example: The launch of the new service was covered by every paper.
senses.exampleCN: 新服务的发布被各家报纸报道。
senses.why: English often turns a forceful verb into a noun, so the moment of release becomes a public event with guests and speeches.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把有力的动词变成名词，于是「放出的那一刻」成了有来宾和致辞的公开活动。

intro.en: Launch goes back to a Latin word for a spear, and the idea of hurling something forward runs through all of its senses.
intro.cn: launch 可追到拉丁语中表示长矛的词，而「把东西向前掷出」这个意思贯穿它的所有义项。

items.en: Lancea meant a light spear, the weapon carried by a lancer.
items.cn: lancea 指轻矛，是长矛手使用的武器。

items.en: Lanceare meant to wield a lance, and in French the sense widened to throwing or driving something forward.
items.cn: lanceare 意为挥动长矛，在法语中词义扩大到把东西向前投出或推动。

items.en: Old French lanchier meant to hurl a spear or to set a boat afloat, and English borrowed both ideas.
items.cn: 古法语 lanchier 意为投掷矛枪或让船下水，英语把这两种意思都借了过来。

items.en: Middle English launch kept the movement sense: to let something go forward, whether a boat, a weapon or a shout.
items.cn: 中古英语 launch 保留「向前放出」的意思：无论是船、武器还是一声喊。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from ships to rockets and businesses, so launch now starts almost anything.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从船扩展到火箭与企业，于是 launch 几乎能「启动」任何东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the lance family and its built forms; the near-meaning group collects verbs for beginning or releasing something.
note.cn: 形近组收 lance 一词族及其构成形式；近义组收表示开始或放出的动词。

entries.definition: A device or person that sends something into the air.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物送上天空的装置或人。

entries.definition: The platform from which a rocket leaves the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 火箭升空所依托的平台。

entries.definition: A long spear, the weapon behind the word.
entries.definitionCN: 长矛，是这个词背后的武器。

entries.definition: To begin doing or making something.
entries.definitionCN: 开始做或开始制造某物。

entries.definition: To set a process or plan going.
To let something go out or become available.
entries.definitionCN: 放出某物或使其可获取。

entries.definition: To shoot a weapon or set off a rocket.
entries.definitionCN: 射击武器或点火发射火箭。

normalIntro.en: A spear thrown forward is the oldest picture inside this word, and every later sense repeats the same release.
normalIntro.cn: 一支向前掷出的长矛是这个词里最古老的画面，此后每个义项都在重复同一次「放出」。

normal.en: Latin lancea is a spear, and lanceare means to use one, which is the physical core of launch.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lancea 是长矛，lanceare 是使用长矛，这就是 launch 的物理核心。

normal.en: A ship is launched down a slipway, driven forward like a thrown weapon.
normal.cn: 船沿滑道下水，像被掷出的武器一样被推向前方。

normal.en: A product launch borrows the same gesture: something built inside is pushed out into the market.
normal.cn: 产品发布借用同一个动作：在内部造好的东西被推向市场。

normal.en: A rocket launch repeats the old throw upward, with fire instead of muscle.
normal.cn: 火箭发射重复了古老的向上投掷，只是用火代替了肌肉。

normal.en: Launcher and launchpad name the tool and the place that make the release possible.
normal.cn: launcher 与 launchpad 指让这次「放出」得以发生的工具和地点。

abstract.en: One verb covers ships, rockets and businesses because all three must leave the place where they were built.
abstract.cn: 一个动词涵盖船、火箭与企业，因为三者都必须离开自己被造出来的地方。

abstract.en: A launch is a public moment because release is risky: once it is out, it must float without help.
abstract.cn: 发布是公开的时刻，因为放出有风险：一旦出去，它必须自己浮着。

abstract.en: The lance became a satellite, but the gesture is still a throw.
abstract.cn: 长矛变成了卫星，可那个动作仍然是一次投掷。

examples.en: The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
examples.cn: 船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。

examples.en: The company will launch its new phone next month.
examples.cn: 公司下个月将推出新手机。

examples.en: They launched the satellite from a desert site.
examples.cn: 他们在沙漠场地发射了那颗卫星。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「浪起」——浪头起来了，船就下水、火箭就升空；谐音记住 launch 是发射、发起。

root: 源自拉丁语 lancea（长矛）与 lanceare（挥矛），经古法语 lanchier（投矛、使船下水）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is something thrown forward; it becomes a ship sliding into water, a rocket rising, and a product sent into the market.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是把东西向前掷出；它化为滑入水中的船、升空的火箭，以及推向市场的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dock gates open and a new hull slides down the slipway into the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：船坞闸门打开，新船体沿滑道冲入水中。

branches.en: a hull sliding down greased timbers
branches.cn: 船体沿涂油的木滑道下滑

branches.en: a crowd watching a ferry enter the water
branches.cn: 人群看着渡轮入水

branches.en: a phone shown on a stage for the first time
branches.cn: 手机第一次在台上亮相

branches.en: a rocket clearing the tower
branches.cn: 火箭飞离发射塔

branches.en: newspapers reporting a service launch
branches.cn: 报纸报道一项服务的发布

intro.en: A Latin spear and its verb pass through French into English, and English adds -er and a compound to name the tools of release.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「矛」及其动词经法语进入英语，英语又加 -er 和复合成分来命名放出的工具。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 立即的；直接的；紧接的
definition_en: happening at once, or nearest in relation, with nothing in between
core_image: 手机屏幕上跳出一条消息和一个红色的立即回复按钮
scene: 客服台前的铃声响了一声，值班的人就转身接起。 The patient's illness was immediate, so there was no time to look up the file first.
sceneCN: 这里 immediate 意思是「立即的」（第 1 个义项：不隔时间的），句意是那人的病情紧急，来不及先调资料。画面里有铃响一声就转身的值班人。

pos.zh: 形容词：立即的、直接的、紧接的

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: occurring without delay, with no waiting time
senses.definitionCN: 毫无拖延、没有等待时间地发生
senses.example: The medicine brought immediate relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这药立刻缓解了症状。
senses.why: The Latin prefix means without, and the root means in between, so immediate describes a gap that simply is not there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀意为「没有」，词根意为「中间」，于是 immediate 描述的是根本不存在的间隔。

senses.title: Direct and without a middle step
senses.definition: coming from or acting on something with no intermediary
senses.definitionCN: 不经中间环节地来自或作用于某物
senses.example: Smoking is an immediate cause of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟是这种病的直接原因。
senses.why: If nothing lies between cause and result, the link is immediate, exactly as the root says.
senses.whyCN: 若因果之间不夹任何东西，这条链就是「直接」的，正是词根所说的意思。

senses.title: Nearest in place or time
senses.definition: closest in the surrounding area or in the near future
senses.definitionCN: 在周边环境或近期中最靠近的
senses.example: The immediate area was cleared for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一带被清空了两个小时。
senses.why: The nearest ring around a point has nothing between it and that point, so the same word covers physical closeness.
senses.whyCN: 围绕一点最近的圈与那点之间没有东西，于是同一个词也覆盖了空间上的近。

intro.en: Immediate is built from Latin in-, not, and mediatus, intervened, so the word literally means with nothing in between.
intro.cn: immediate 由拉丁语 in-（不）与 mediatus（介入）构成，字面意思就是「中间没有东西」。

items.en: Mediare meant to be in the middle, from medius, the word for middle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mediare 意为居间，源自 medius，即「中间的」。

items.en: Adding in- produced immediatus, describing what has nothing standing between.
items.cn: 加上 in- 构成 immediatus，形容中间不夹任何东西的状态。

items.en: Schoolmen used immediatus of the direct relation between God and the soul.
items.cn: 经院学者用 immediatus 形容神与灵魂之间的直接关系。

items.en: In philosophy the word named knowledge received without proof or medium.
items.cn: 在哲学中这个词指不经证明或媒介而得的认识。

items.en: English took immediate broadly, for instant action, direct causes and the nearest circle of people.
items.cn: 英语广泛采用，用于即时行动、直接原因与最亲近的那圈人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the medi- middle root; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is prompt.
note.cn: 形近组收带 medi-「中间」词根的词；近义组收表示迅疾的词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, meaning at once.
Lying in the middle, the exact opposite of having no gap.
entries.definitionCN: 居于中间的，与「无间隔」正好相反。

entries.definition: A middle thing or channel, from the same middle root.
entries.definitionCN: 中介物或媒介，同出「中间」词根。

entries.definition: Happening in a single moment, often used of products.
entries.definitionCN: 一瞬间发生的，常用于产品。

entries.definition: Done quickly and without being late.
Without anyone or anything in between.
entries.definitionCN: 中间没有人或物隔着的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks open up the literal sense: no mediator, no gap, nothing in the middle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把字面意思摊开：没有中介、没有空隙、中间没有东西。

normal.en: Im- is not, medi- is middle, so immediate is not-middle, with nothing between.
normal.cn: im- 是不，medi- 是中间，所以 immediate 就是「不隔中间」。

normal.en: Compare intermediate: add the middle and you get the opposite.
normal.cn: 对照 intermediate：加上「中间」就成了反义。

normal.en: Four beats, stress the second: im-ME-di-ate.
normal.cn: 四个拍子，重音在第二：im-ME-di-ate。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and becomes the word on every emergency sign.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 成副词，就是每个应急告示上的那个词。

normal.en: Immediate family is the small circle with no relatives standing between you and them.
normal.cn: 直系亲属就是与你之间不夹旁人的那一小圈。

abstract.en: The word measures distance of a special kind: not metres, but the absence of anything in between.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量一种特殊的距离：不是米数，而是「中间空无一物」。

abstract.en: Direct causes and instant replies share one quality, the refusal of a middle step.
abstract.cn: 直接原因与即时应答共享一种性质：拒绝中间那一步。

abstract.en: Everything immediate is short-lived; the word names a moment that cannot be stored.
abstract.cn: 一切「立即」都短暂；这个词命名的是一刻无法储存的时间。

examples.en: The order takes immediate effect.
examples.cn: 该命令立即生效。

examples.en: His immediate reaction was to say nothing.
examples.cn: 他的第一反应是一言不发。

examples.en: Only the immediate family was invited to the ceremony.
examples.cn: 只有直系亲属受邀参加仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + medi 中间 + ate——中间不隔任何东西：立即的；直接的

root: 拉丁语 medius「中间」→ mediare「居间」，加否定 in- 成 immediatus，近代进入英语作 immediate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: no delay in time, no step in between, and no distance around.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：时间上不拖延、环节上不夹中介、空间上紧邻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flashing message with a red reply button waiting to be pressed.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上闪烁的消息和待按的红色回复键。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: immediate relief and immediate effect share a zero delay.
branches.cn: 时钟线：立刻缓解与立即生效都是零延迟。

branches.en: THE CHAIN LINE: an immediate cause needs no link before it.
branches.cn: 链条线：直接原因前面不需要再加一环。

branches.en: THE RING LINE: the immediate area and the immediate family are the closest ring.
branches.cn: 圆圈线：附近一带与直系亲属都是最内那一圈。

branches.en: THE GAP LINE: both senses depend on the same missing middle.
branches.cn: 间隙线：两种用法都依赖同一个「缺席的中间」。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST LINE: intermediate words do the opposite job.
branches.cn: 对照线：带 intermediate 的词正做相反的事。

intro.en: Immediate is a prefix plus a middle root plus a participle ending, a clean case of literal meaning surviving.
intro.cn: immediate 是前缀、中间词根与分词词尾的组合，字面义至今完好。

latinIntro.en: Medius and the negative in- are standard Latin, and immediatus is attested in later Latin.
latinIntro.cn: medius 与否定前缀 in- 是标准拉丁成分，immediatus 在后世拉丁文献中可见。

items.exampleCN: medium 与 mediate 共用此根。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，表示具备某性质
不隔中间，立即的、直接的

items.example: An intermediate class runs on Fridays.

items.exampleCN: 调解人与双方都见了面。

definition_zh: 漫游；徘徊；闲逛；走神；偏离（正题、路线）
definition_en: to walk around slowly without a clear purpose or direction, or to let thoughts drift
core_image: 没有目的地的脚步：风往哪吹，人就往哪走
scene: 傍晚的老城巷子，灯光一盏盏亮起。 After dinner she wandered through the old streets without any plan.
sceneCN: 这里 wander 是「闲逛」（第 1 个义项：无目的地漫游）；句意是晚饭后她在老街间随意漫步，没有既定安排。

pos.zh: 动词：漫游；徘徊；闲逛；走神；偏离

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「漫游者、流浪者」，由动词加施动者后缀构成
形容词，义为「漫游的、蜿蜒的」，由现在分词转作定语
名词，义为「漫游欲、旅行癖」，由 wander 加德语 Lust（欲望）构成

senses.title: To walk without purpose
senses.titleCN: 闲逛：没有目的地的步行
senses.definition: to walk around slowly and aimlessly, for pleasure or from restlessness
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而随意地四处走动，或为消遣，或因躁动
senses.example: After dinner she wandered through the old streets without any plan.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她在老街间随意漫步，没有既定安排。
senses.why: Middle English wandren meant to stray from the path; steps without a goal keep straying.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 wandren 意为偏离路径；没有目标的脚步一直在「偏」。

senses.title: To move off course
senses.definition: to move away from a route, place, or proper position
senses.definitionCN: 离开既定路线、地点或应有的位置
senses.example: The sheep wandered from the flock and got lost.
senses.exampleCN: 那只羊离了羊群，走丢了。
senses.why: Straying is the core image: the path exists, but feet choose elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 「走偏」是核心意象：路明明在那里，脚却选择了别处。

senses.title: To lose concentration
senses.definition: to let thoughts drift away from the matter at hand
senses.definitionCN: 让思绪从眼前之事漂移开去
senses.example: His mind wandered during the long lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的讲座中，他的思绪走神了。
senses.why: The mind has paths too; attention that strays is attention that wanders.
senses.whyCN: 思绪也有路径，注意力一「走偏」，便是走神。

senses.title: To drift through places over time
senses.titleCN: 漂泊：长时段、长距离的流转
senses.definition: to travel from place to place over a long period without a fixed home
senses.definitionCN: 长时期辗转各地，没有固定的居所
senses.example: He wandered the world for a decade before settling down.
senses.exampleCN: 他漂泊了十年才安定下来。
senses.why: One stray after another, stretched over years, becomes a life without a fixed path.
senses.whyCN: 一次次的偏离延伸成年月，便成了没有固定路径的人生。

senses.title: A curve or slow stretch
senses.titleCN: 蜿蜒：路径或话语的曲折
senses.definition: of a path, river, or talk, to proceed in a slow, curving, indirect way
senses.definitionCN: 指小路、河流或谈话缓慢、弯曲、迂回地进行
senses.example: The river wanders across the plain in slow bends.
senses.exampleCN: 河流在大平原上蜿蜒缓行。
senses.why: A path that never goes straight keeps straying from the direct line.
senses.whyCN: 从不走直线的路径，便是在不断偏离直线。

intro.en: Wander comes from Old English wandrian, to move about aimlessly, of Germanic origin, possibly related to wend and wind.
intro.cn: wander 源自古英语 wandrian（无目的地走动），属日耳曼来源，一般认为可能与 wend（转向）和 wind（蜿蜒）相关。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind wandrian involves turning and winding movement; its wider links are generally believed rather than proven.
items.cn: wandrian 背后的重构词根涉及转弯与蜿蜒的移动；其更宽泛的同源联系属于普遍推定。

items.en: Wandrian means to wander, journey about, or stray from the path.
items.cn: 古英语 wandrian 意为游荡、四处行走、偏离路径。

items.en: Wandren keeps the senses of aimless motion and straying from the right way.
items.cn: 中古英语 wandren 保留「无目的移动」与「偏离正路」两义。

items.en: The sense extends to wandering minds, wandering rivers, and wandering peoples.
items.cn: 15 至 16 世纪，词义扩展到走神的思绪、蜿蜒的河流与迁徙的民族。

items.en: German Wanderlust forms inside the same family, borrowed back into English for the love of roaming.
items.cn: 19 世纪，德语 Wanderlust 在同一词族内构成，又被英语借回，指对漫游的热爱。

items.en: Wander now covers feet, rivers, minds, and planets, from wandering off to wandering stars.
items.cn: 如今 wander 涵盖脚步、河流、思绪与行星，从走散到「游星」皆有此词。

note.en: Wander stands at the center of its Germanic straying family; look-alikes share the root and spelling traps, near meanings share the field of aimless motion.
note.cn: wander 处于日耳曼「游荡」词族中心：形近组共享词根与拼写陷阱，近义组共享「无目的移动」义场。

entries.definition: a person who wanders, a rover
entries.definitionCN: 漫游者；由 wander 加施动者后缀构成

entries.definition: a strong desire to travel and roam
entries.definitionCN: 旅行癖；由 wander 加德语 Lust 构成

entries.definition: to feel curiosity or doubt; a marvel
entries.definitionCN: 好奇、疑惑、奇迹；与 wander 仅一字母之差，词源不同，是最经典的易混词

entries.definition: to go in a particular direction, slowly
entries.definitionCN: 缓缓前行；一般认为与 wander 同源相关

entries.definition: to follow a winding course
entries.definitionCN: 迂回行进；源自小亚细亚一条曲折河流的名字，词源与 wander 不同

entries.definition: to walk for pleasure, or to talk at length without focus
entries.definitionCN: 漫步、闲谈离题；兼指脚与嘴的漫游

entries.definition: to move about widely over an area
to walk in a slow, relaxed way
entries.definitionCN: 散步、闲逛；强调轻松，不强调无方向

entries.definition: to move slowly without direction, carried by forces
entries.definitionCN: 漂移；多用于水、雾、人群与思绪

entries.definition: to move away from the group or the correct path
entries.definitionCN: 走失、偏离；强调离开应有的位置

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic straying family and its famous spelling twin.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自日耳曼「游荡」词族及其著名的拼写孪生词。

normal.en: the root means to stray from the path; wandering is one long stray.
normal.cn: 词根意为偏离路径；wandering 就是一次长长的偏离。

normal.en: wander has an a, wonder has an o: feet wander, minds wonder.
normal.cn: wander 有 a，wonder 有 o：脚会 wander（游荡），心会 wonder（好奇）。

normal.en: wanderlust is German-built: wander plus Lust, desire to roam.
normal.cn: wanderlust 是德语造词：wander 加 Lust（欲望），即漫游之欲。

normal.en: wander off is the phrase for straying away or daydreaming.
normal.cn: wander off 既指走散，也指走神。

normal.en: wandering stars was an old name for planets that drift across the sky.
normal.cn: wandering stars（游星）是古人对行星的称呼，因其漂移于星空。

abstract.en: A paper boat left on a stream goes where the current likes.
abstract.cn: 放在溪流上的纸船，去往水流喜欢去的地方。

abstract.en: A path drawn in pencil, curved and erased and curved again.
abstract.cn: 一条用铅笔画出的路径，弯了又擦，擦了又弯。

abstract.en: In class your eyes stay on the board while your feet walk invisible roads.
abstract.cn: 课堂上眼睛盯着黑板，脚却在走看不见的路。

examples.en: We wandered around the market all morning, tasting whatever looked good.
examples.cn: 整个上午我们在集市里闲逛，见到想吃的就尝一口。

examples.en: The conversation wandered from weather to old school days.
examples.cn: 谈话从天气漫游到旧日校园。

examples.en: A stray cat wandered into the yard and stayed for years.
examples.cn: 一只流浪猫游荡进了院子，一住就是好几年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 wander ≈ 万得」——「万得自在」，想去哪就去哪，千般路线任你选。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古英语 wandrian（游荡）。

root: 日耳曼语词根（一般认为与 *wend-「转向」相关）→ 古英语 wandrian（无目的地游荡、偏离路径）→ 中古英语 wandren → 现代英语 wander。与 wend（前行）可能同源；注意与 wonder（好奇，源自古英语 wundor）词源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: From straying steps outward: aimless walking, losing the route, drifting minds, years of roaming, and the slow curves of rivers and talk.
sensesIntro.cn: 从偏离的脚步向外铺开：漫无目的的走、迷路的偏、走神的心、经年的漂泊，最后到河流与谈话的蜿蜒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps that keep choosing anywhere but the straight line
core.cn: 核心意象：脚步总在选择直线以外的任何方向

branches.en: The root pleasure: walking with nowhere to be
branches.cn: 根本的乐趣：无处可去之地的闲步

branches.en: The stray and the curve: off route, winding on
branches.cn: 偏离与蜿蜒：离了路线，弯着前行

branches.en: The mind's own wandering: attention off its path
branches.cn: 思绪的游荡：注意力偏离其路径

branches.en: Strays stretched over years become a roving life
branches.cn: 偏离延伸成年月，便成漂泊人生

branches.en: Homeless motion, from evening stroll to lifetime journey
branches.cn: 无居所的移动，从傍晚闲逛到一生行旅

intro.en: The Germanic straying root builds mostly compounds and agent nouns in modern English.
intro.cn: 日耳曼「游荡」词根在现代英语中主要构成复合词与施动名词。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic; Latin has no direct cognate in the wander-family.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼来源，wander 词族中没有直接的拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 幸存；存活；残存物
definition_en: the state of continuing to live or exist
core_image: 荒岛上的一顶小帐篷，旁边还燃着一小堆火
scene: 在寒冷的海水中，生存需要极大的勇气。 Survival in the cold sea required great courage.
sceneCN: 这里 survival 是「幸存」（第 1 个义项）；句意：在寒冷的海水中，生存需要极大的勇气。

senses.title: Continuing to live
senses.definition: the state of continuing to live through danger
senses.definitionCN: 经历危险后继续存活的状态
senses.example: Survival in the cold sea required great courage.
senses.exampleCN: 在寒冷的海水中，生存需要极大的勇气。
senses.why: This is the core sense of staying alive.
senses.whyCN: 这是「活下来」的核心义项。

senses.title: Something that has lasted
senses.definition: a custom or object that has continued from an earlier time

definition_en: an open container with a handle for carrying liquid

scene: 井边的石板还湿着。 He filled the bucket from the well.

senses.title: A container with a handle
senses.definition: an open round container with a handle for liquid

definition_en: a sign or object that stands for something else
core_image: 广场上白鸽飞起，人们立刻想到和平
scene: 鸽子是和平的象征。 The dove is a symbol of peace.
sceneCN: 这里 symbol 是「象征」（第 1 个义项）；句意：鸽子是和平的象征。

senses.title: A sign standing for an idea
senses.definition: a thing that represents a quality or idea
senses.definitionCN: 代表某种品质或观念的事物
senses.example: The dove is a symbol of peace.
senses.exampleCN: 鸽子是和平的象征。
senses.why: The word began with a token broken in two, whose halves proved identity when rejoined.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一分为二的信物，两半合起便证明身份。

senses.title: A written or printed sign

senses.example: The symbol for water is H2O in chemistry.

senses.example: She became a symbol of courage for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这座小镇勇气的象征。
senses.why: A thing can stand for an idea, and so can a person, which extends the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 物能代表观念，人也能，这沿用了同一个逻辑。

definition_zh: 领主；勋爵；贵族；上帝；巨头
definition_en: a man of noble rank or high office; also a title for God and for a dominant figure
core_image: 一名男子站在长桌尽头，把一条条面包分给排队的家人
scene: 中世纪的庄园里，天还没亮，管家已经把当天要分的面包摆上长桌。 The lord of the manor watched as each family received its share of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 lord 是「领主、庄园主」（第 2 个义项：封建领主）；句意为庄园领主看着每户人家领到属于自己的那份面包。画面里可认出长桌、面包和排队的人。

pos.zh: 领主；勋爵；贵族；上帝；巨头

derivatives.zh: 由 lord 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「贵族般的；高傲的」
由 lord 加抽象名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「领主身份；统治权」
由 land 与 lord 复合而成，义为「地主；房东」
由 over 与 lord 复合而成，义为「最高领主；霸主」

senses.title: A nobleman or a title of rank
senses.definition: a man who holds a noble title, or the title used before his name
senses.definitionCN: 拥有贵族头衔的男子，或用于其名字前的尊称
senses.example: The king granted the title of lord to his most loyal soldier.
senses.exampleCN: 国王把勋爵头衔授予他最忠诚的士兵。
senses.why: In feudal society the word marked a man who held land and rank above ordinary people, so it settled into a formal title.
senses.whyCN: 在封建社会，这个词标记着拥有土地、地位高于平民的男子，于是逐渐固定为一种正式头衔。

senses.title: A feudal master who owns land and controls those who work it
senses.definition: a man who owns land and has power over the people living and working on it
senses.definitionCN: 拥有土地并支配在其上生活、劳作之人的男子
senses.example: The lord of the manor collected rent from every family on his land.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园领主向地上的每一户人家收取地租。
senses.why: The same word for a title also named the practical power behind it: land, rent and the labour of other people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示头衔的词也指头衔背后的实际权力：土地、地租和别人的劳作。

senses.title: God, or Christ, in religious use
senses.definition: a title used for God or for Christ in Christian speech and prayer
senses.definitionCN: 基督教言语和祈祷中对上帝或基督的称呼
senses.example: They prayed to the Lord for guidance before the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前他们向上帝祈求指引。
senses.why: The Bible was translated into English with this word for a master, so the everyday term for a powerful man was lifted to name the highest power.
senses.whyCN: 《圣经》英译时用这个表示「主人」的词，于是这个日常用来指有权势之人的词被提升去指最高的权能者。

senses.title: A dominant figure in a particular field
senses.definition: a man who is very powerful or influential in a particular activity or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在某一活动或行业中极有权势或影响力的人物
senses.example: He is a lord of the fashion world, with shops in every capital.
senses.exampleCN: 他是时装界的巨头，在每个首都都有店铺。
senses.why: From owning land the word widened to owning influence, so a man who ruled an industry could be called its lord.
senses.whyCN: 从拥有土地扩展到拥有影响力，于是统治一个行业的人也可以被称为该行业的霸主。

intro.en: Lord began as a compound for the keeper of the bread, then grew into a word for masters, nobles and God.
intro.cn: lord 最初是「看管面包的人」的复合词，后来发展为指主人、贵族与上帝。

items.en: The word is first recorded as hlāfweard, a compound of hlāf, bread, and weard, keeper.
items.cn: 这个词最早记作 hlāfweard，由表示面包的 hlāf 与表示看守者的 weard 复合而成。

items.en: Everyday speech shortened hlāfweard to hlāford, and the middle sounds were swallowed.
items.cn: 日常口语把 hlāfweard 缩成 hlāford，中间的音节被吞掉了。

items.en: Middle English lord kept the meaning of a household head and a man of authority.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lord 保留「一家之主」与「有权势的男子」两层意思。

items.en: Under feudalism the word became a title for landowners and nobles, and later for members of the House of Lords.
items.cn: 在封建制度下，这个词成为地主与贵族的头衔，后来又指上议院的成员。

items.en: Modern English uses lord for nobles, for masters, and as a religious title for God.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lord 指贵族、主人，也用作对上帝的宗教称呼。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from the same bread-and-keeper compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for masters and rulers.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「面包＋看守者」复合词衍生出的词；近义组收表示主人与统治者的词。

entries.definition: The female counterpart of lord, from a compound meaning bread-kneader.
entries.definitionCN: lord 的女性对应词，源自表示「揉面包的人」的复合词。

entries.definition: A shaped mass of baked bread, from the same Old English word for bread.
entries.definitionCN: 一条烤好的面包，来自同一个古英语「面包」词。

entries.definition: Guarding, or a guarded area, from the keeper element in lord.
entries.definitionCN: 守护或受监护的区域，来自 lord 中「看守者」那一部分。

A man who has control over people or a household.
