normalIntro.en: The word is a compressed compound: bread plus keeper. Its family keeps returning to guarding, owning and ranking above others.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是被压缩的复合词：面包加看守者。它的同族词反复回到看管、拥有与高人一等。

normal.en: Lord began as hlāfweard, the keeper of the bread, so the first lord was simply the one who fed the household.
normal.cn: lord 最初写作 hlāfweard，即看管面包的人，所以最早的领主不过是供养全家的人。

normal.en: The middle of hlāfweard was lost in speech, which is why lord looks nothing like loaf or ward today.
normal.cn: hlāfweard 中间的音在口语里消失了，所以今天的 lord 看起来和 loaf、ward 都不像。

normal.en: Lady is its female counterpart, built from a word for kneading bread, so both titles come from the kitchen.
normal.cn: lady 是它的女性对应词，来自表示揉面包的词，所以两个头衔都出自厨房。

normal.en: Landlord adds land to lord: the man who owns the land and the building on it.
normal.cn: landlord 在 lord 前加 land，指拥有土地及其上房屋的人。

normal.en: Lordship adds -ship: the rank or power that belongs to a lord.
normal.cn: lordship 加后缀 -ship，指属于领主的身份或权力。

abstract.en: A word that once meant the man guarding the bread shows how food was the first form of power.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指「看管面包的人」的词，说明食物是最初的权力形式。

abstract.en: From feeding a household to ruling a country, the same word simply changed the size of the table.
abstract.cn: 从供养一家人到统治一个国家，同一个词只是换了桌子的尺寸。

abstract.en: Calling God lord keeps the oldest human image of power: someone above who provides and protects.
abstract.cn: 称上帝为 lord，保留了人类最古老的权力形象：在上方供给并保护的人。

examples.en: The lord of the manor watched as each family received its share of bread.
examples.cn: 庄园领主看着每户人家领到属于自己的那份面包。

examples.en: They prayed to the Lord for guidance before the journey.
examples.cn: 出发前他们向上帝祈求指引。

examples.en: The young noble was granted the title of lord after the battle.
examples.cn: 那位年轻贵族战后被授予勋爵头衔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老得」——上了年纪、德高望重的老爷，就是 lord。

root: 古英语 hlāfweard（hlāf「面包」+ weard「看守者」）缩合为 hlāford，再演变为 lord；一般认为与「供养、看管家宅」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a man with power over land and people; the senses branch into a noble title, a feudal master, God, and a dominant figure in a field.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是握有土地与人身权力的男子；义项分出贵族头衔、封建领主、上帝，以及某一领域的巨头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man at the end of a long table, handing out bread to a waiting household.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名男子站在长桌尽头，把面包分给等待的众人。

branches.en: a ceremony where a title is formally granted
branches.cn: 正式授予头衔的仪式

branches.en: a manor where rent is collected from tenants
branches.cn: 向佃户收取地租的庄园

branches.en: hands folded in prayer before a long journey
branches.cn: 长途出发前合拢的祈祷之手

branches.en: a fashion house with shops in every capital
branches.cn: 在每个首都都有店铺的时装帝国

branches.en: the same man holding a title and the land that pays for it
branches.cn: 同一个人既拥有头衔，又拥有供养头衔的土地

intro.en: Lord is a worn-down compound of two Old English nouns, and later English built new words on it with -ly, -ship and further compounding.
intro.cn: lord 是两个古英语名词磨损而成的复合词，后来的英语又用 -ly、-ship 和再次复合造出新词。

latinIntro.en: Lord comes from Germanic bread-and-keeping words, so it has no reliable Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: lord 来自日耳曼语表示面包与看守的词，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.example: Old English hlāf survives in the modern word loaf.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 hlāf 保存在现代英语的 loaf 里。

items.example: The weard stood at the door of the hall.
Hlāford named the man who guarded the family's bread.
items.exampleCN: hlāford 指为全家看管面包的人。

items.meaning: a woman of rank or the female head
items.example: The lady of the house greeted the guests.

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词和副词的后缀
items.example: Lordly means noble or proud, built with this suffix.
items.exampleCN: lordly 意为贵族般的或高傲的，由这个后缀构成。

items.example: Lordship means the rank or power of a lord.
items.exampleCN: lordship 指领主的身份或权力。

items.meaning: owner of land or rented property
items.example: The landlord raised the rent last spring.
items.exampleCN: 房东去年春天涨了房租。

items.meaning: the rank, power or territory of a lord
items.example: The lordship passed to his eldest son.
items.exampleCN: 领主之位传给了他的长子。

definition_zh: 评论说；谈论；注意到；评论
definition_en: to say something that shows what you have noticed, or the words you say
core_image: 眼睛在人群里忽然停住，指着某处说了一句话
scene: 她翻到照片最后一页，忽然说这地方她小时候来过。 She turned to the last page and remarked that she had been there as a child.
sceneCN: 这里 remark 是「评论说」（第 1 个义项：说出自己注意到的事）；句意：她翻到最后一页，评论说自己小时候去过那里。

derivatives.zh: remark 加 -able 构成，义为「非凡的；值得注意的」
remarkable 加 -ly 构成，义为「非凡地；出乎意料地」

senses.title: To say something about what you notice
senses.definition: to say something, often briefly, as a comment on what you have seen or heard
senses.definitionCN: 就所见所闻简短地说出看法
senses.example: He remarked that the room was unusually quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他说这房间安静得反常。
senses.why: The French source means to mark, so the core picture is noticing a detail and then pointing it out in words.
senses.whyCN: 法语词源意为「做标记」，所以核心画面是先注意到某个细节，再用话语把它指出来。

senses.title: To notice something
senses.definition: to see or notice something and mentally mark it as important
senses.definitionCN: 看到或注意到某事，并在心里把它标记为重要
senses.example: She remarked a strange smell as she entered.
senses.exampleCN: 她进门时注意到一股奇怪的气味。
senses.why: Before a remark can be spoken it must be marked in the mind, which is the older layer of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 话未出口先在心里做标记，这正是这个动词更古老的一层含义。

senses.title: A spoken or written comment
senses.definition: a short statement that gives an opinion or draws attention to something
senses.definitionCN: 表达看法或引起注意的简短话语
senses.example: His opening remarks were short and warm.
senses.exampleCN: 他的开场白简短而温暖。
senses.why: The noun keeps the same mark: a remark is a small marker placed on a topic by the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留同一个「标记」：评论就是说话者在话题上留下的小标记。

intro.en: Remark comes from French remarquer, to mark or note, built on re- and marquer.
intro.cn: remark 来自法语 remarquer「标记、注意」，由 re- 与 marquer 构成。

items.en: The mark family probably goes back to a Germanic root for a boundary or sign.
items.cn: 表示「标记」的这组词一般认为可追溯到日耳曼语中表示边界或记号的词根。

items.en: Marquer means to mark, and remarquer means to mark out or notice.
items.cn: 古法语 marquer 表示做记号，remarquer 表示标出或注意到。

items.en: Remarquer develops the sense of saying something that one has noticed.
items.cn: remarquer 发展出「就注意到的事说一句」的含义。

items.en: English remark first means to notice, then to utter a comment.
items.cn: 英语 remark 先表示「注意到」，随后表示「说出评论」。

items.en: The noun remark settles into the sense of a short comment or a formal opening address.
items.cn: 名词 remark 固定为简短评论或正式开场白的含义。

note.en: Remark belongs to the mark family and gives us remarkable, while comment is its closest everyday partner.
note.cn: remark 属于 mark 词族，并派生出 remarkable；comment 是它最接近的日常近义词。

entries.definition: unusual and worth noticing
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的；值得注意的，由 remark 加 -able 构成

entries.definition: in a surprising or unusual way
a visible sign or spot
entries.definitionCN: 记号；痕迹，是 remark 的词根来源

entries.definition: a spoken or written opinion about something
entries.definitionCN: 评论；意见，与 remark 名词义几乎同义

entries.definition: to notice something and sometimes mention it
entries.definitionCN: 观察；评论说，兼具看与说

entries.definition: to speak about something briefly
entries.definitionCN: 提到；说起，不强调评论色彩

normalIntro.en: Remark is literally to mark again in the mind before marking it in words.
normalIntro.cn: remark 字面上是先在心中再做一个标记，然后用话语标出来。

normal.en: Re- plus mark gives marking something so that it stands out.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 mark，就是给它做个记号让它显出来。

normal.en: Remarkable is what deserves a remark, and remarkably tells how it was done.
normal.cn: remarkable 是值得被评论的，remarkably 说明是以何种方式做到的。

normal.en: Remarks in the plural often means a formal speech at an opening.
normal.cn: 复数 remarks 常指开幕时的正式致辞。

normal.en: The verb is usually followed by that or on.
normal.cn: 这个动词后面通常接 that 从句或 on。

normal.en: A casual remark can still carry a lot of weight.
normal.cn: a casual remark 随口一说，也可能很有分量。

abstract.en: Imagine a finger pointing at a small detail and a voice naming it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指指向某个细节，同时有个声音把它说出来。

abstract.en: See a pencil making a small tick beside a line of text.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔在文字旁划出一个小小的勾。

abstract.en: Think of a guest standing up to say a few words at a table.
abstract.cn: 想一位客人在餐桌旁站起来说几句话。

examples.en: She remarked on how much the town had changed.
examples.cn: 她谈到这座小镇变化有多大。

examples.en: He made a rude remark and left the room.
examples.cn: 他留下一句粗鲁的话就离开了房间。

examples.en: The chair opened the meeting with a few remarks.
examples.cn: 主席以几句开场白开始了会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞马克」——在瑞丽买一枚马克笔，边看边做记号；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 remarquer（标记、注意），由 re-（再次）与 marquer（做记号）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Marking a detail in the mind and marking it in words produce the senses of noticing, saying, and the comment itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 在心里标记一个细节、再用话语标记它，就生出「注意到」「说道」以及「评论」三个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes stopping on a detail, then a voice naming it.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光在某个细节上停住，随后有个声音把它说出来。

branches.en: A marked detail is spoken aloud, which is the everyday verb.
branches.cn: 被标记的细节被说出来，就是最日常的动词用法。

branches.en: Before speech there is silent marking, the older sense of noticing.
branches.cn: 说话之前先有无声的标记，即更古老的「注意到」。

branches.en: The words left behind are themselves the mark, hence the noun.
branches.cn: 留下的那些话本身就是记号，于是有了名词用法。

branches.en: Saying and the thing said are two sides of one mark.
branches.cn: 说出来的动作与被说出的内容，是同一个标记的两面。

branches.en: Noticing is the gate through which every remark passes.
branches.cn: 「注意到」是每一句评论都必须经过的门。

intro.en: Remark is a French verb that entered English with both its prefix and its root intact.
intro.cn: remark 是带着前缀与词根一起进入英语的法语动词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of again, and the mark root carries the sense of a sign or boundary.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 增添「再次」的意思，mark 词根带有「记号、边界」的含义。

items.example: Re- marks the action as repeated or emphatic.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让动作带上重复或强调的意味。

items.example: The mark root also gives the English word mark.
items.exampleCN: mark 词根也产生了英语单词 mark。

items.example: Marquer is the French verb behind remark.
items.exampleCN: marquer 是 remark 背后的法语动词。

items.example: Remarquer is borrowed almost whole into English.
items.exampleCN: remarquer 几乎被整体借入英语。
remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」。

items.example: Marker shows the plain mark root with an agent ending.
items.exampleCN: marker 展示了 mark 词根加施事词尾的形态。

items.meaning: an easily seen feature of a landscape
items.example: Landmark joins land with the same marking root.
items.exampleCN: landmark 把 land 与同一个标记词根组合起来。

definition_zh: 以前的；先前的；上一个的；以前的（所有者等）
definition_en: existing or happening before something else, especially immediately before
core_image: 一条路上留下的一串脚印：你已经走过的那一段
scene: 会议开始前，主持人先翻开旧纪要。 The chair read the minutes of the previous meeting first, so that everyone remembered what had been decided last time.
sceneCN: 这里 previous 是「上一次的、先前的」（第 2 个义项：紧接在这一次之前的那一次）；句意：主持人先读了上一次会议的纪要，让大家记起上次决定了什么。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、旧纪要、日历、文件夹、投影幕；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 以前的；先前的；上一个的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Happening before in time
senses.definition: existing or occurring earlier than something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: Previous studies reached a different conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的研究得出了不同结论。
senses.why: Latin praevius means 'going before', from prae- 'before' and via 'way'. The word pictures something that has already travelled the road you are now on.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevius 意为“走在前面的”，由 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”构成。这个词描绘已经走完你脚下这段路的东西。

senses.title: Immediately preceding
senses.definition: the one directly before the current one
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着当前这个之前的那个
senses.example: The previous chapter explained the method.
senses.exampleCN: 上一章解释了方法。
senses.why: English often uses the word for the nearest predecessor, not any earlier item. The road image narrows to the step just behind your heel.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用它指最近的前一个，而非任何更早的项。道路意象收窄到脚跟后的那一步。

senses.title: Former, no longer current
senses.definition: holding a position or relationship no longer held
senses.definitionCN: 担任的职位或关系已不再持续
senses.example: The previous owner kept the garden beautiful.
senses.exampleCN: 前任主人把花园打理得很美。
senses.why: When attached to a role or person, the word marks a slot that has changed hands. What is previous is not merely earlier but replaced.
senses.whyCN: 当它附着于角色或人时，标记一个已经易手的槽位。previous 不只是更早，而是已被取代。

senses.title: Earlier in a sequence or order
senses.definition: coming earlier in an ordered series
senses.definitionCN: 在有序序列中更早出现
senses.example: Check the previous entry in the log.
senses.exampleCN: 检查日志中的前一条。
senses.why: Sequences let 'before' be counted: the previous item is the one at index n-1. The spatial image of the road becomes an ordered list.
senses.whyCN: 序列让“在前”可以计数：previous 项就是索引 n-1 的那一项。道路的空间意象变成有序列表。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase previous to
senses.definition: in formal usage, earlier than or before
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：早于、在……之前
senses.example: Previous to 1900, the town had no railway.
senses.exampleCN: 1900 年以前，这个镇没有铁路。
senses.why: The phrase turns the adjective into a preposition. It is more formal than 'before' and slightly archaic in speech, but common in legal and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把形容词变成介词。它比 before 正式，口语中略古旧，但在法律与历史写作中常见。

senses.title: Premature or hasty (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, happening too soon, before the proper time
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：发生得过早，早于适当时间
senses.example: a previous conclusion, drawn before the evidence
senses.exampleCN: 证据未齐就作出的过早结论
senses.why: The word once carried the sense 'too early', not only 'earlier'. The Latin comparative idea of going ahead could imply jumping the gun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾有“过早”而非仅仅“更早”的意思。拉丁语“走在前面”的比较意味，可以暗指抢跑。

senses.title: The antecedent term (logic)
senses.definition: in logic, the premise or term that comes before another
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中先于另一项的前提或词项
senses.example: The previous proposition must be established first.
senses.exampleCN: 前一个命题必须先被确立。
senses.why: Logic orders propositions in a chain. The previous proposition is the ground on which the next stands, so priority becomes inference.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把命题排成链。前一个命题是后一个站立的地面，于是“在先”变成推理关系。

senses.title: Already mentioned or known
senses.definition: already referred to earlier in a text or conversation
senses.definitionCN: 在文本或谈话中已被提及
senses.example: The previous example shows the pattern clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 前面的例子清楚展示了这个模式。
senses.why: Reference needs a backward pointer. The word tells the reader to look up the road already travelled, which is why it is so common in academic prose.
senses.whyCN: 指称需要一个向后指的箭头。这个词让读者回望已经走过的路，所以它在学术写作中如此常见。

intro.en: Previous is a road word: Latin praevius 'going before' combines prae- 'before' with via 'way'. English borrowed it in the 17c. and made it the ordinary adjective for the step just behind.
intro.cn: previous 是一个道路词：拉丁语 praevius“走在前面的”把 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”结合。英语在 17 世纪借入，并让它成为指“刚过去那一步”的常用形容词。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English with the sense 'going before in time or order'.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早在英语中记录为“在时间或次序上在前”之义。

items.en: From Latin praevius 'leading the way, going before' = prae- 'before' + via 'way, road'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 praevius“引路、走在前”= prae-“在前”+ via“道路”。

items.en: via also yields deviate, obvious, trivial, convey, and voyage. The family is about roads, and 'before on the road' is the core of previous.
items.cn: via 还生成 deviate、obvious、trivial、convey、voyage。这个词族关乎道路，而“路上在前”正是 previous 的核心。

items.en: The word settles into its modern sense, especially 'the one immediately before'.
items.cn: 这个词稳定在现代义，尤其指“紧接在前的那一个”。

items.en: The prepositional phrase previous to becomes common in formal prose in the 18c.
items.cn: 介词短语 previous to 在 18 世纪正式书面语中变得常见。

items.en: Modern English prefers before in speech and keeps previous to for legal and historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语口语偏好 before，法律与历史写作保留 previous to。

note.en: The first group shares the via or -vious shape; the second is about adjectives that also mean earlier.
note.cn: 第一组共享 via 或 -vious 的形态，第二组看同样表示“更早”的形容词。

entries.definition: at an earlier time. It is previous plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以前；先前。它是 previous 加 -ly。

entries.definition: clear, literally 'in the way'. It uses the same via.
entries.definitionCN: 明显的，字面“挡在路上”。它用同一个 via。

entries.definition: to go off the way. It is de- 'away from' + via.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离道路。它是 de-“离开”+ via。

entries.definition: earlier or more important. It is stronger and more formal than previous.
entries.definitionCN: 更早或更重要的。它比 previous 更强、更正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past holder of a role. It contrasts with 'latter'.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或某角色的前任。它与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming just before in order. It is the precise word for the item at n-1.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它是指 n-1 项的确切词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin via 'road', the praevius image of going before, the previous/prior/former trio, and the phrase previous to.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 via“道路”、praevius“走在前面”的意象、previous/prior/former 三词的区别，以及短语 previous to。

normal.en: Via means 'road'. Previous things have already walked the road you are on.
normal.cn: via 意为“道路”。previous 的东西已经走过你脚下的路。

normal.en: Prae- means 'before'. Put the two together and you get 'going before on the way'.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”。两者相加就是“在路上走在前面”。

normal.en: Previous vs prior: previous is the everyday 'last one'; prior is formal and can also mean 'more important'.
normal.cn: previous 与 prior：previous 是日常的“上一个”，prior 更正式，还可表示“更重要”。

normal.en: Previous vs former: former contrasts with latter in a pair; previous can point to any earlier item.
normal.cn: previous 与 former：former 在一对中与 latter 相对；previous 可指任何更早的项。

normal.en: Previous to is a formal preposition: lawyers and historians use it, everyday speech says before.
normal.cn: previous to 是正式介词：律师与历史学家用它，日常口语说 before。

abstract.en: Memory is the road behind us: to call something previous is to locate it on that road, not merely to date it.
abstract.cn: 记忆是我们身后的路：称某物 previous，就是把它定位在那条路上，而不只是给它标日期。

abstract.en: Every present moment defines its predecessor, so 'previous' is a relational word disguised as a time word.
abstract.cn: 每个当下都在定义它的前一刻，所以 previous 是一个伪装成时间词的关系词。

abstract.en: The past is not one thing: previous, former, and prior cut it differently, by nearness, role, and rank.
abstract.cn: 过去不是一整块：previous、former、prior 按近远、角色与等级把它切成不同的段。

examples.en: The previous meeting lasted three hours.
examples.cn: 上一次会议开了三个小时。

examples.en: She had no previous experience in teaching.
examples.cn: 她此前没有教学经验。

examples.en: Previous to that year, the village had no school.
examples.cn: 在那一年之前，这个村子没有学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞威士”——扑向前一个瑞威士（路标）→ previous 先前的、上一个

root: 拉丁语 praevius“走在前面的”，由 prae-“在前”+ via“道路”构成；同族有 deviate、obvious、trivial、convey。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of previous, all placed on a road behind the present. The road can be time (last year), a list (the item before), a role (the former owner), or a text (the example above).
sensesIntro.cn: previous 的八个义项都放在当下身后的一条路上。这条路可以是时间（去年）、列表（前一项）、角色（前任）或文本（上面的例子）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the stretch of road already walked.
core.cn: 核心意象：已经走过的那一段路。

branches.en: BEFORE: earlier in time, with an archaic note of 'too early'.
branches.cn: 在前：时间上更早，古义带“过早”色彩。

branches.en: JUST BEFORE: the nearest predecessor in a sequence or list.
branches.cn: 紧邻在前：序列或列表中最近的前一项。

branches.en: FORMER: a role or owner that has been replaced.
branches.cn: 前任：已被取代的角色或所有者。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: previous to turns the adjective into a formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：previous to 把形容词变成正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: REFERENCE: in logic and texts, the earlier item grounds or points back.
branches.cn: 指称：在逻辑与文本中，前项提供依据或向后指。

intro.en: Previous is an adjective from Latin praevius. English adds -ly and -ness, and the same via builds deviate, obvious, and convey.
intro.cn: previous 是来自拉丁 praevius 的形容词。英语加 -ly 与 -ness，同一个 via 还构成 deviate、obvious、convey。

latinIntro.en: Latin praevius 'going before' combines prae- 'before' with via 'way'. The via family is large: deviate, obvious, trivial, convey, voyage. All keep the image of a road.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praevius“走在前”把 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”结合。via 词族很大：deviate、obvious、trivial、convey、voyage。它们都保留道路意象。

items.meaning: to leave the road; to depart from a norm
a departure from a route or standard

items.structure: from Old French voiage, from via
items.meaning: a journey by sea or space

definition_zh: 癌症；恶性肿瘤；社会毒瘤
definition_en: a serious disease in which cells grow in an uncontrolled way
core_image: 身体里不受控地增生的细胞
scene: 她陪父亲去医院复查。 The doctor explained how cancer spreads.
sceneCN: 这里 cancer 是「癌症」（第 1 个义项：细胞失控增生的疾病）；句意是医生解释了癌症如何扩散。

pos.zh: 名词：社会毒瘤，蔓延的弊端

derivatives.zh: 癌性的，像癌一样蔓延的

senses.title: The disease of uncontrolled cells
senses.definition: a disease in which abnormal cells divide without control
senses.definitionCN: 异常细胞不受控制地分裂增生的疾病
senses.example: The doctor explained how cancer spreads.
senses.exampleCN: 医生解释了癌症如何扩散。
senses.why: The core image is a growth spreading through the body like a crab's legs.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是像蟹足一样在体内蔓延的肿块。

senses.title: A spreading social evil
senses.definition: a harmful practice that spreads through a society
senses.definitionCN: 在社会中蔓延的有害现象
senses.example: Greed is a cancer in the system.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是体制里的一颗毒瘤。
senses.why: A disease that spreads became a picture for any spreading harm.
senses.whyCN: 会扩散的疾病，被用来比喻任何蔓延的祸害。

intro.en: Cancer is the Latin word for crab, given to tumours that spread like claws.
intro.cn: cancer 是拉丁语里的「螃蟹」，因肿瘤蔓延像蟹足而得名。

items.en: karkinos meant crab and also named such tumours.
items.cn: 希腊语 karkinos 意为螃蟹，也用来指这类肿瘤。

items.en: cancer meant crab and took over the medical sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cancer 意为螃蟹，并承接了医学义。

items.en: cancer appears in early medical writing.
items.cn: 古英语的医学文献中已出现 cancer。

items.en: The word was fixed for malignant growths.
items.cn: 十七世纪起固定指恶性肿瘤。

items.en: Cancer names the disease and any spreading evil.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cancer 兼指这种疾病与蔓延的祸害。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cancer base; the near-meaning group gives related medical words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cancer 词基；近义组是相关的医学词。

entries.definition: affected by or like cancer
a substance that can cause cancer
able to cause cancer
an abnormal growth of cells
of a growth, likely to spread and be dangerous
a state of being unwell

normalIntro.en: Cancer is Latin for crab, a picture of claws spreading.
normalIntro.cn: cancer 是拉丁语的螃蟹，取蟹足蔓延之象。

normal.en: The plural is cancers.
normal.cn: 复数是 cancers。

normal.en: Lung cancer is a common phrase.
normal.cn: lung cancer 是常见搭配。

normal.en: Cancerous adds -ous.
normal.cn: cancerous 加了后缀 -ous。

normal.en: Carcinogen keeps the Greek root.
normal.cn: carcinogen 保留希腊词根。

normal.en: The word also means a spreading evil.
normal.cn: 这个词也指蔓延的祸害。

abstract.en: See a crab's legs reaching across a page.
abstract.cn: 想象蟹足伸过一页纸。

abstract.en: See cells dividing again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象细胞一次次分裂。

abstract.en: See a dark stain spreading through cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象污渍在布上不断扩散。

examples.en: The doctor explained how cancer spreads.
examples.cn: 医生解释了癌症如何扩散。

examples.en: She lost her uncle to lung cancer.
examples.cn: 她的叔叔死于肺癌。

examples.en: Greed is a cancer in the system.
examples.cn: 贪婪是体制里的一颗毒瘤。

dict_mnemonic.text: cancer 的 can 像螃蟹的钳子，cer 像横着爬的脚，钳子一张一合，正是螃蟹也是癌的拉丁名。

root: cancer 直接借自拉丁语 cancer（螃蟹），对应希腊语 karkinos；古代医生见肿瘤周围血管如蟹足伸展，便用螃蟹命名这种病。

sensesIntro.en: The disease of spreading cells, and any spreading social harm.
sensesIntro.cn: 细胞扩散的疾病，以及任何蔓延的社会祸害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: claws reaching outward through tissue.
core.cn: 核心意象：蟹足在组织里向外伸展。

branches.en: lung cancer
branches.cn: 肺癌

branches.en: cancer cells
branches.cn: 癌细胞

branches.en: treat cancer
branches.cn: 治疗癌症

branches.en: cancer research
branches.cn: 癌症研究

branches.en: a cancer in the system
branches.cn: 体制里的毒瘤

intro.en: Cancer forms an adjective with -ous and technical words with carcin-.
intro.cn: cancer 能加 -ous 构成形容词，也能用 carcin- 构成专业词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin cancer, a crab.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 cancer，意为螃蟹。

items.meaning: the basic unit of the body

definition_zh: 永久的；长期不变的；常设的；正式编制的；（烫发）保持较久的
definition_en: lasting for a very long time or indefinitely; not temporary
core_image: 石碑上凿出的字，雨水冲了几十年还在
scene: 河岸的界桩深深打进岩层，涨水也没能把它拔起。 The border marker is a permanent fixture on the bank.
sceneCN: 这里指长期存在、不会自行消失（第 1 个义项：永久或长期存续的）；句意为这块界标是河岸上永久固定的设施；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 永久的；长期的；常设的；正式编制的

senses.title: Lasting indefinitely
senses.definition: lasting forever or with no fixed end
senses.definitionCN: 永远存在或没有确定终点
senses.example: The treaty made the river a permanent boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 条约使这条河成为永久边界。
senses.why: Latin permanere means to remain through to the end, and the present participle fixes that staying into a quality.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 permanere 意为「一直留到最后」，现在分词把这层「留住」定成品性。

senses.title: Long-lasting rather than temporary
senses.definition: intended to last a long time, in contrast with a temporary arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 打算长期维持，与临时安排相对
senses.example: They moved into a permanent office after the trial year.
senses.exampleCN: 试行一年后，他们搬进了长期办公室。
senses.why: Everyday use softens forever into for the foreseeable future.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把「永远」软化为「可预见的将来」。

senses.title: A regular staff position
senses.definition: holding a post with a settled contract rather than a short-term one
senses.definitionCN: 持有稳定合同的岗位，而非短期岗位
senses.example: She was offered a permanent post in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 系里给了她一个正式职位。
senses.why: Employment law turns the word into a boundary between contract types.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法把这个词变成合同类型之间的界限。

senses.title: A material that does not fade
senses.definition: marking a material whose colour or mark is meant to stay
senses.definitionCN: 标记一种颜色或印记不易消失的材料
senses.example: He labelled the box with a permanent marker.
senses.exampleCN: 他用不褪色记号笔在箱子上做了标记。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the arrangement to the stuff that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从安排转到承载安排的材质上。

senses.title: A long-holding wave
senses.definition: a hairstyle whose curl is meant to last for months
senses.definitionCN: 卷发效果能维持数月的发型
senses.example: She asked the stylist for a permanent before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出行前她请理发师给她烫个发。
senses.why: The trade noun keeps the promise of duration in a small everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 行业里的名词把「持久」的承诺放进一个日常小义。

senses.title: A resident status
senses.definition: the legal right to live in a country without time limit
senses.definitionCN: 在一国无限期居住的合法权利
senses.example: He applied for permanent residence after five years.
senses.exampleCN: 五年后他申请了永久居留。
senses.why: Immigration law needs a term for the strongest form of stay.
senses.whyCN: 移民法需要一个词指最稳固的居留形式。

senses.title: Irreversible harm
senses.definition: damage that will not heal or be undone
senses.definitionCN: 不会痊愈或被撤销的损害
senses.example: The frost caused permanent damage to the buds.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻对花芽造成了永久性损害。
senses.why: The word marks the point where repair stops being possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出修复不再可能的那一点。

senses.title: A lasting record
senses.definition: an official record that is kept indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 无限期保存的正式记录
senses.example: The offence stayed on his permanent record.
senses.exampleCN: 这项过错留在了他的永久档案里。
senses.why: Bureaucracy uses the word to say that erasure is not allowed.
senses.whyCN: 行政系统用这个词表示不允许抹除。

intro.en: Permanent comes from Latin permanens, the present participle of permanere, to remain throughout, built on per- through and manere to stay. Both parts are clear.
intro.cn: permanent 来自拉丁 permanens，即 permanere「一直留到最后」的现在分词，由 per-「贯穿」与 manere「停留」构成。两部分都清楚。

items.en: Manere meant to stay, remain or dwell, and it also gives mansion and manor through French.
items.cn: manere 意为停留、留下、居住，经法语也给出 mansion 与 manor。

items.en: Per- means through or throughout, so permanere is to stay through the whole span.
items.cn: per- 意为贯穿、始终，因此 permanere 是在整段时间里一直留下。

items.en: The present participle permanens described a thing that keeps its place or state.
items.cn: 现在分词 permanens 描述保持位置或状态的事物。

items.en: English took permanent in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入 permanent，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Permanence and permanency name the state, while impermanent adds a Latin negative prefix.
items.cn: permanence 与 permanency 命名状态，impermanent 则加拉丁否定前缀。

items.en: The word now also names a hairstyle, a marker and a residence status.
items.cn: 这个词如今还指一种发型、一种记号笔与一种居留身份。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stay-root; the second group names duration and stability.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「停留」词根；第二组是表示持续与稳定的近义说法。

entries.definition: The state of lasting or remaining unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 持久或保持不变的状态。

entries.definition: In a way that is meant to last.
entries.definitionCN: 以打算长久维持的方式。

entries.definition: Not lasting; the negative form built with im-.
entries.definitionCN: 不持久的；用 im- 构成的否定形式。

entries.definition: To stay behind or continue in a place, from the same Latin verb through French.
entries.definitionCN: 留下或继续在某处，经法语出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A large house, from the Latin idea of dwelling.
entries.definitionCN: 大宅，出自拉丁语「居住」的观念。

entries.definition: Continuing for a long time, without implying forever.
Lasting through hardship or time.
entries.definitionCN: 历经困难或时间仍持续。

entries.definition: Continuing without interruption, often stronger than permanent.
entries.definitionCN: 不间断地持续，语气常比 permanent 更强。

entries.definition: Set in place and not changing.
Steady and not likely to move or fail.

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Manere is to stay, and per- is through, so permanent is to stay through the whole span.
normal.cn: manere 是停留，per- 是贯穿，所以 permanent 是整段时间都留下。

normal.en: Mansion and manor come from the same dwelling word.
normal.cn: mansion 与 manor 出自同一个「居住」词。

normal.en: Impermanent is the negative: im- plus permanent.
normal.cn: impermanent 是反义：im- 加 permanent。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: permanent residence, permanent job, permanent damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：永久居留、正式工作、永久损害。

normal.en: A permanent marker keeps its mark; a permanent wave keeps its curl.
normal.cn: 不褪色记号笔留住字迹，烫发留住卷度。

abstract.en: Permanent is a stone carved with letters that outlast the hand that cut them.
abstract.cn: 永久是石头上凿的字，比刻字的手活得更久。

abstract.en: The word promises duration without naming an end, which is why lawyers argue over it.
abstract.cn: 这个词承诺持续却不说明终点，所以律师总要争它。

abstract.en: To call a thing permanent is to bet that time will not revise it.
abstract.cn: 称某物为永久，就是赌时间不会改写它。

examples.en: The bridge was built as a permanent crossing, not a seasonal one.
examples.cn: 这座桥建成永久通道，而非季节性设施。

examples.en: A permanent loss of hearing followed the explosion.
examples.cn: 爆炸之后出现了永久性听力丧失。

examples.en: The museum keeps a permanent collection in the east wing.
examples.cn: 博物馆在东翼设有永久藏品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泼门能特」——门泼上漆也烂不掉：永久的

root: 拉丁 permanens「一直留下的」← permanere「留到最后」← per-「贯穿」+ manere「停留、居住」。manere 经法语也给出 mansion 与 manor；英语中世纪晚期借入 permanent，确切首见年代不确定。permanence 指状态，impermanent 由 im- 否定；现代另有烫发、不褪色记号笔与永久居留等专义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from endless duration to long arrangements, posts, materials, hairstyles, statuses, harm and records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从无限持续，转到长期安排、职位、材料、发型、身份、损害与档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters cut into stone, still readable after decades of rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：凿进石头的字，几十年雨水之后仍可辨认。

branches.en: THE ENDLESS STAY: duration with no fixed end.
branches.cn: 没有终点的停留：没有确定终点的持续。

branches.en: THE LONG ARRANGEMENT: what is meant to outlast a trial period.
branches.cn: 长期安排：打算熬过试行期的安排。

branches.en: THE SETTLED STATUS: a staff post and a residence right.
branches.cn: 稳固的身份：正式职位与居留权利。

branches.en: THE FIXED MARK: ink that does not fade and a curl that holds.
branches.cn: 固定的印记：不褪的字迹与持久的卷度。

branches.en: THE UNCHANGING RECORD: harm that cannot be undone and a file that is never erased.
branches.cn: 不可改的记录：无法撤销的损害与永不抹除的档案。

intro.en: Permanent is Latin permanens plus the English adjective ending; the verb permanere carries both per- and manere.
intro.cn: permanent 是拉丁 permanens 加英语形容词词尾；动词 permanere 同时带着 per- 与 manere。

latinIntro.en: Manere gives the stay-root, per- carries it through time, and permanens supplies the participle behind the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: manere 提供「停留」词根，per- 让它贯穿时间，permanens 提供英语形容词背后的分词。

items.example: The prefix stretches the stay across the whole span.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把「停留」拉满整段时间。

items.example: The verb is the plain act of remaining.
items.exampleCN: 动词就是「留下」这一平实动作。

items.structure: Latin verb, compound of per- and manere
items.example: Latin joined the two parts into one verb.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把两部分合成一个动词。

items.example: The participle turns the act into a quality.
The noun names the state the participle describes.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名分词所描述的状态。

items.example: English keeps the participle ending as -ent.
items.exampleCN: 英语把分词词尾保留为 -ent。

items.example: The noun is the abstract partner of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词是形容词的抽象搭档。

items.example: The adverb marks how long something is meant to stay.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出打算维持多久。

items.example: The prefix makes impermanent, the negative partner.
items.exampleCN: 前缀构成 impermanent 这一否定搭档。

items.example: The negative keeps the same stay-root.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式沿用同一「停留」词根。

definition_zh: 企业；事业；进取心
definition_en: a business or bold project, or the initiative needed to undertake one
core_image: 一队人带着工具走出城门，去把一桩有风险的大事做成
scene: 小镇上那家做太阳能板的企业去年雇了三十名工人。 The enterprise that makes solar panels in the town hired thirty workers last year.
sceneCN: 这里 enterprise 是「企业」（第 1 个义项：从事经营活动的组织）；句意：镇上那家生产太阳能板的企业去年雇了三十名工人。

derivatives.zh: 有进取心的；有事业心的

senses.title: A business organization
senses.definition: a company or business, especially a commercial one
senses.definitionCN: 公司或商业组织，尤指营利性的
senses.example: The family runs a small printing enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人经营着一家小型印刷企业。
senses.why: An enterprise is first something undertaken, and a business is the most common thing undertaken in modern life.
senses.whyCN: enterprise 本指「所承担之事」，而现代生活中最常见的承担之事就是经营。

senses.title: A bold or difficult project
senses.definition: an ambitious project that involves effort and risk
senses.definitionCN: 需要付出努力并承担风险的宏大计划
senses.example: Building the bridge was a bold enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 修建这座桥是一项大胆的事业。
senses.why: The original French noun names something undertaken, so any large risky task fits.
senses.whyCN: 法语原名词指「着手去做的事」，因此任何宏大而冒险的任务都符合。

senses.title: Initiative and boldness
senses.definition: the quality of being willing to start new and difficult things
senses.definitionCN: 愿意开创全新而困难之事的品质
senses.example: She showed great enterprise in opening the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她开这家店，表现出很强的进取心。
senses.why: The willingness to undertake is abstracted into a personal quality.
senses.whyCN: 「敢于承担」被抽象为一种个人品质。

intro.en: Enterprise comes from Old French entreprise, something undertaken, from entreprendre, to take in hand, built on Latin inter and prehendere.
intro.cn: enterprise 来自古法语 entreprise（所承担之事），源于 entreprendre（着手去做），由拉丁语 inter 与 prehendere 构成。

items.en: Inter means between or among.
items.cn: inter 意为在……之间。

items.en: Prehendere means to seize or take hold of.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握住。

items.en: Entreprendre means to undertake or take in hand.
items.cn: entreprendre 意为着手、承担。

items.en: Entreprise names the thing undertaken.
items.cn: entreprise 指所承担的事情。

items.en: Middle English enterprise covers bold deeds as well as business.
items.cn: 中古英语 enterprise 既指大胆行动，也指商业经营。

items.en: Modern English separates the business, project, and initiative senses.
items.cn: 现代英语分化出企业、事业与进取心三个义项。

note.en: Enterprise is an undertaking noun, and it sits near its own derivatives and near words for business and ventures.
note.cn: enterprise 是一个「承担之事」名词，与自身派生词以及表示商业和冒险事业的词相邻。

entries.definition: willing to start new and bold things
a person who starts a business
the activity of starting businesses
a company or commercial activity
an organization that sells goods or services
a new project involving risk

normalIntro.en: Enterprise contains prise, from French prendre, to take: it is the taking up of a task.
normalIntro.cn: enterprise 含有 prise，来自法语 prendre（拿取）：它就是「把事情接过来做」。

normal.en: Entre- means between, and prendre means take: taking something in hand.
normal.cn: entre- 表示之间，prendre 表示拿取：把事情接到手里。

normal.en: A business enterprise is an undertaking that must pay its way.
normal.cn: 商业企业是一项必须自己养活自己的事业。

normal.en: Spirit of enterprise names the courage to start something risky.
normal.cn: spirit of enterprise 指敢于开创冒险之事的勇气。

normal.en: Entrepreneur is the person, while enterprise is the thing or the quality.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 是人，enterprise 是事情或品质。

normal.en: Compare venture: both involve risk, but enterprise also means a company.
normal.cn: 对比 venture：两者都含风险，但 enterprise 还可指公司。

abstract.en: Picture a group setting out at dawn with tools and a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人带着工具和地图，在黎明出发。

abstract.en: Imagine a merchant signing a contract on a busy quay.
abstract.cn: 想象一位商人在繁忙的码头上签下合同。

abstract.en: Think of a seed pushed into hard ground before any shoot appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被按进硬土，嫩芽尚未出现。

examples.en: The family runs a small printing enterprise.
examples.cn: 这家人经营着一家小型印刷企业。

examples.en: Building the bridge was a bold enterprise.
examples.cn: 修建这座桥是一项大胆的事业。

examples.en: She showed great enterprise in opening the shop.
examples.cn: 她开这家店，表现出很强的进取心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enter prize」——敢进场去拿奖，就是有进取心的事业；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（之间）＋ prehendere（抓取）→ 古法语 entreprendre（着手做）→ entreprise（所承担之事）→ 中古英语 enterprise → 现代英语 enterprise。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins as something taken in hand, then narrows to a business, widens to any bold project, and finally names the courage behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词最初指「接到手里的事」，随后收窄为商业企业，又扩展为任何大胆事业，最后指背后的勇气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group setting out to take a risky task in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人出发，把有风险的任务接到手里。

branches.en: A business is the most concrete modern undertaking.
branches.cn: 企业是现代社会最具体的「承担之事」。

branches.en: A bold project keeps the original sense of something undertaken.
branches.cn: 大胆事业保留「所承担之事」的原义。

branches.en: Initiative is the personal quality that starts undertakings.
branches.cn: 进取心是开创事业所需的个人品质。

branches.en: A company and a large project both require planning and risk.
branches.cn: 公司与大型项目都需要规划与冒险。

branches.en: Bold projects exist because someone supplies the initiative.
branches.cn: 大胆事业之所以存在，是因为有人提供进取心。

intro.en: Enterprise is a French noun built from entre and prendre, with English endings forming its modern family.
intro.cn: enterprise 是由 entre 与 prendre 构成的法语名词，现代词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, and prehendere means to seize; French entreprendre joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 表示之间，prehendere 表示抓取；法语 entreprendre 把两者结合。

items.example: Inter is the Latin source of entre-.
items.exampleCN: inter 是 entre- 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Prehendere is the deep root of prendre.
items.exampleCN: prehendere 是 prendre 的深层词根。

items.example: Entreprendre means to take something in hand.
items.exampleCN: entreprendre 意为把事情接到手里。

items.example: Entreprise is the direct source of enterprise.
items.exampleCN: entreprise 是 enterprise 的直接来源。
enterprise 保留「承担之事」的含义。

senses.title: A building for plays
senses.definition: a building with a stage where plays are performed
senses.definitionCN: 设有舞台、用于演出戏剧的建筑
senses.example: We watched a play at the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在戏院看了一出戏。
senses.why: The Greek root meant the place for viewing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根本义即「观看之场所」。

senses.title: The art of drama
senses.definition: the art or world of writing and performing plays
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧创作与表演的艺术或行业
senses.example: She has worked in the theatre for years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在戏剧界工作多年。
senses.why: The place of viewing becomes, by habit, the art viewed.

senses.title: A cinema or similar hall
senses.definition: a hall for films or lectures, especially in American use

senses.example: The old theatre now shows films.

senses.why: A hall built for viewing serves any show worth watching.
senses.whyCN: 为观看而建的厅堂可服务任何值得看的演出。

intro.en: Theatre comes from Greek theatron, a place for viewing.
intro.cn: theatre 源自希腊语 theatron（观看之所）。

items.en: The root thea- meant to see.
items.cn: 印欧词根 thea- 意为观看。

items.en: Theatron meant the seating of a hillside theatre.
items.cn: 希腊语 theatron 指山坡剧场座位。

items.en: Theatrum kept the same meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语 theatrum 义同。

items.en: Theatre passed into French.
items.cn: 经古法语 theatre 传入。

items.en: Theatre meant both the building and the art.
items.cn: 14 世纪 theatre 兼指建筑与戏剧艺术。

note.en: Theatre is compared with look-alike words and with places of show.
note.cn: 把 theatre 与形近词及演出场所作对比。

sensesIntro.cn: theatre 从观看的厅堂延伸到戏剧艺术与电影放映厅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tiered seats facing a lit stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：面向亮起舞台的层层看台。

branches.en: The building is the primary sense.

branches.en: The hall lends its name to the art.
branches.cn: 厅堂之名转借给艺术。

branches.en: The theatre world means drama people.

branches.en: Film halls reuse the viewing hall.
